```ts
/**
 * 3e: an account's case in lane 2 that holds one rule report under R4 about its handle, unanswered, with a snapshot
 * whose handle is the one the profile holds now unless told otherwise, and the account's standing. `live` is the handle
 * the profile holds now; `snapped` the one the newest snapshot copied.
 */
export function retireCase(live = "Ada_L", snapped = "Ada_L", standing: Partial<CaseStanding> = {}): CaseView {
  const base = accountCase();
  const [copied] = base.snapshots;
  if (!copied || copied.withheld) throw new Error("the account case's snapshot shows its content");
  return accountCase({
    id: CASE_RETIRE,
    lane: 2,
    stateVersion: 1,
    intakeSeq: 1,
    suspicion: null,
    target: { type: "account", id: ACCOUNT_ID, handle: live, displayName: "Ada", bio: "", deleted: false },
    snapshots: [{ ...copied, authorHandle: snapped, handle: snapped, displayName: "Ada", bio: "" }],
    items: [item({ id: ITEM_RETIRE, ruleId: "R4", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS", link: "http://localhost:8081/u/ada_l" })],
    history: [],
    standing: { ...NO_ACCOUNT_STANDING, ...standing },
  });
}

export function orderCase(overrides: Partial<CaseView> = {}): CaseView {
  return postCase({
    id: CASE_ORDER,

    items: [
      item({
        id: ITEM_ORDER,
        seq: 1,
        position: 1,
```

```tsx
    expect(refused).toMatch(/link still works/);
    expect(refused).not.toMatch(/password manager by hand|asked to remove/);
    for (const out of [synced, noPin, refused]) {
      expect(out).not.toMatch(/passkey_/);
      expect(out).toContain("<button");
    }
  });

  test("a dead link or a full set of keys leaves nothing to try", () => {
    for (const code of ["staff_enrollment_invalid", "staff_key_limit"]) {
      const out = html(<EnrollView {...base} result={{ ok: false, code, status: 400, cleanup: "none" }} />);
      expect(out, code).not.toContain("<button");
    }
  });

  const registered = (name: string) => ({ ok: true as const, key: { id: "5b0e4a52-3c1d-4f6e-9a8b-7c6d5e4f3a2b", name, createdAt: "2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z", lastUsedAt: null }, credentialId: "bmV3LWtleQ" });

  test("a registered key's name is text, and the page signs in with that key itself, never through the sign-in page", () => {
    for (const name of [HOSTILE.script, HOSTILE.img, HOSTILE.bidi]) {
      const out = html(<EnrollView {...base} result={registered(name)} />);
      expect(out).toMatch(/Sign in with it once/);
      expect(out).toContain(">Sign in with this key</button>");
      // The sign-in page would show home to a browser that already holds a staff session, and ask no key.
      expect(out).not.toContain('href="/signin"');
      expect(out).not.toMatch(/<(script|img)\b/);
      expect(out).toContain(`<bdi>`);
    }
  });

  test("the check after the enrolment: under way, opened the console, or failed with the operator to tell", () => {
    const busy = html(<EnrollView {...base} result={registered("Blue key")} check={{ state: "busy" }} />);
    expect(busy).toMatch(/<button[^>]*disabled=""[^>]*aria-busy="true"|<button[^>]*aria-busy="true"[^>]*disabled=""/);
    const opened = html(<EnrollView {...base} result={registered(HOSTILE.script)} check={{ state: "opened" }} />);
    expect(opened).toMatch(/opened the console/);
    expect(opened).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    expect(hrefs(opened)).toEqual(["/"]);
    expect(opened).not.toContain(">Sign in with this key</button>");
    const failed = html(<EnrollView {...base} result={registered("Blue key")} check={{ state: "failed", message: "This key does not open the staff console." }} />);
    expect(failed).toContain("This key does not open the staff console.");
    expect(failed).toMatch(/tell the operator at once/);
    // The person may try again: a closed prompt is no verdict on the key.
    expect(failed).toContain(">Sign in with this key</button>");
  });
});

    // The page read its session at 09:00 and its person kept acting, so the idle timer never read /me again: the session
    // the page holds still says 09:00 when Home opens at 20:00.
    const pageOpened = Date.parse("2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z");
    const homeOpened = Date.parse("2026-10-01T20:00:00.000Z");
    const at = (createdAt: string, seq: number): AuditEntry => ({ ...signIn("mod_anna", seq), createdAt });
    const fake = fakeFetch({
      "GET /api/staff/me": [{ status: 200, body: makeMe({ at: pageOpened }) }, { status: 200, body: makeMe({ at: homeOpened, absolute: 3600 }) }],
      "GET /api/staff/audit?action=staff_sign_in": {
        status: 200,
        body: {
          entries: [
            at("2026-10-01T19:00:00.000Z", 40),
            at("2026-09-24T20:30:00.000Z", 39),
            // Older than 7 days at 20:00, though not at the page's stale 09:00: the list ends before it.
            at("2026-09-24T19:30:00.000Z", 38),
            at("2026-09-24T09:30:00.000Z", 37),
          ],
          nextCursor: 37,
        },
      },
      "GET /api/staff/sessions": { status: 200, body: { sessions: [] } },
      "GET /api/staff/keys": { status: 200, body: { keys: [] } },
      "GET /api/staff/overview": { status: 200, body: QUIET },
    });
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "" });
    const store = createConsoleStore({ api, clock: new FakeClock(), path: "/", history: { pushState: noop, replaceState: noop } });
    await store.start();
    const held = store.get().session;
    if (held.kind !== "signed-in") throw new Error("the page holds no session");
    expect(serverNow(held.me)).toBe(pageOpened);

    // What the screen runs when it opens, with the session the page holds as its `me`.
    let signIns: Loadable<AuditEntry[]> = { state: "loading" };
    openHome(api, { current: true }, { overview: noop, signIns: (value) => (signIns = value), sessions: noop, keys: noop });
    await settle();
    expect(signIns).toMatchObject({ state: "ready" });
    const out = html(<HomeView {...props} me={held.me} signIns={signIns} />);
    expect(out).toContain("2026-10-01 19:00");
    expect(out).toContain("2026-09-24 20:30");
    expect(out).not.toContain("2026-09-24 19:30");
    expect(out).not.toContain("2026-09-24 09:30");
    // The screen's own /me, marked as its person's opening of it, came before the first page of sign-ins.
    const asked = fake.requests.map((r) => `${r.url} ${r.headers["x-staff-activity"]}`);
    expect(asked.filter((r) => r.startsWith("/api/staff/me"))).toEqual(["/api/staff/me 1", "/api/staff/me 1"]);
    expect(asked.indexOf("/api/staff/audit?action=staff_sign_in 1")).toBeGreaterThan(asked.lastIndexOf("/api/staff/me 1"));
    store.dispose();
  });
});
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/account/deletion.test.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AccountDeps } from "../../src/account/context";
import { confirmDeletion, purge, startDeletion } from "../../src/account/flows/deletion";
import { PURGE_INTERVAL_MS, createPurgeJob, purgePending } from "../../src/account/purge";
import { AuthError, type Session } from "../../src/auth";
import type { RequestContext } from "../../src/auth/context";
import { randomToken, sha256Hex } from "../../src/auth/crypto";
import { MemoryJobLock } from "../../src/lib/jobs";
import { MemoryStore } from "../../src/middleware/rate-limit";

const T0 = 1_789_000_000_000;

interface LogLine {
  level: number;
  msg: string;
  userId?: string;
  purged?: number;
  failed?: number;
}

/**
 * The deletion flows and the purge job on stateful fakes of the three module interfaces: the auth
 * fake knows one account whose handle is "ada" and keeps deleted_at and purged_at per account; the
 * social fake keeps which profiles were purged and can be told to fail once for an account, before its
 * transaction does anything or at its commit (which puts back the image rows the transaction took, as a
 * rollback would); the media fake holds image ids per owner and hands them out once, and can be told to
 * fail a request for files once. Every call is logged in order, the commit of the social purge's
 * transaction included, and the transaction it opens is a sentinel the media fake must be handed.
 */
function harness() {
  let t = T0;
  const calls: string[] = [];
  const lines: LogLine[] = [];
  const users = new Map<string, { deletedAt: Date | null; purgedAt: Date | null }>();
  const purgedProfiles = new Map<string, Date>();
  const failing = new Set<string>();
  const failingCommit = new Set<string>();
  /** 3f: the accounts whose address the auth module holds for a report to the authorities. */
  const held = new Set<string>();
  /** When set, the next request for files fails, as it does while the uploads volume cannot be written. */
  const failingRequest = { once: false };
  const images = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const requested: string[][] = [];
  const started: { session: Session; ctx: RequestContext }[] = [];
  const tx = { sentinel: randomUUID() } as unknown as DbTx;
  const seenTx: unknown[] = [];
  const deps: AccountDeps = {
    auth: {
      startDeletion: async (session, ctx) => {
        calls.push("auth.startDeletion");
        started.push({ session, ctx });
        return { flowId: `flow-${session.userId}` };
      },
      // 3e: a terminated account's take-down; the harness's moderation fake decides when it is called.
      takeDownTerminated: async () => false,
      confirmDeletion: async (session, input) => {
        calls.push("auth.confirmDeletion");
        if (input.handle.toLowerCase() !== "ada") throw new AuthError("invalid_request", 400, "handle_mismatch");
        const user = users.get(session.userId);
        if (!user || user.deletedAt) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
        user.deletedAt = new Date(t);
      },
      pendingPurges: async () => {
        calls.push("auth.pendingPurges");
        return [...users].filter(([, user]) => user.deletedAt && !user.purgedAt).map(([id]) => id);
      },
      finishPurge: async (userId) => {
        calls.push("auth.finishPurge");
        const user = users.get(userId);
        // As the real statement: a row already purged, or never deleted, is left alone. 3f: an address held for a report
        // waits, and the answer says so.
        if (!user?.deletedAt || user.purgedAt) return "none";
        if (held.has(userId)) return "held";
        user.purgedAt = new Date(t);
        return "purged";
      },
      exportAccount: async () => {
        throw new Error("not exercised here");
      },
      appendEvent: async () => undefined,
    },
    social: {
      purgeProfile: async (userId, now, within) => {
        calls.push("social.purgeProfile");
        if (failing.delete(userId)) throw new Error("the social purge failed");
        const rowsBefore = images.get(userId);
        await within(tx);
        if (failingCommit.delete(userId)) {
          calls.push("social.rollback");
          if (rowsBefore) images.set(userId, rowsBefore);
          throw new Error("the social purge's commit failed");
        }
        calls.push("social.commit");
        if (!purgedProfiles.has(userId)) purgedProfiles.set(userId, now);
      },
      exportProfile: async () => {
        throw new Error("not exercised here");
      },
    },
    media: {
      purgeOwner: async (within, ownerId) => {
        calls.push("media.purgeOwner");
        seenTx.push(within);
        const ids = images.get(ownerId) ?? [];
        images.delete(ownerId);
        return ids;
      },
      requestDeletion: async (ids) => {
        calls.push(`media.requestDeletion(${ids.length})`);
        if (failingRequest.once) {
          failingRequest.once = false;
          throw new Error("EROFS: the uploads volume cannot be written");
        }
        requested.push([...ids]);
      },
      exportImages: async () => [],
    },
    limits: new MemoryStore(() => t),
    log: pino({ level: "info" }, { write: (line: string) => void lines.push(JSON.parse(line) as LogLine) }),
    now: () => new Date(t),
  };
  /** An onboarded account, live unless told otherwise, with a session that just proved a credential. */
  function account(options: { deletedAt?: Date; images?: string[] } = {}): { userId: string; session: Session } {
    const userId = randomUUID();
    users.set(userId, { deletedAt: options.deletedAt ?? null, purgedAt: null });
    if (options.images) images.set(userId, options.images);
    const session: Session = {
      sessionId: sha256Hex(randomToken()),
      userId,
      deviceId: randomUUID(),
      role: "user",
      onboarded: true,
      mfaEnabled: false,
      reauthAt: new Date(t),
      handle: randomUUID(),
      factors: { email: t },
      passkeyId: null,
    };
    return { userId, session };
  }
  const ctx: RequestContext = { ipHash: randomToken(), userAgent: "test" };
  return {
    deps,
    calls,
    lines,
    users,
    purgedProfiles,
    failing,
    failingCommit,
    failingRequest,
    held,
    images,
    requested,
    started,
    tx,
    seenTx,
    ctx,
    account,
    now: () => new Date(t),
    advance(ms: number) {
      t += ms;
    },
  };
}

describe("account deletion: the flows", () => {
  test("the start step hands the session and the request context to the auth module and answers its flow id", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account();
    expect(await startDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, h.ctx)).toEqual({ flowId: `flow-${ada.userId}` });
    expect(h.started).toEqual([{ session: ada.session, ctx: h.ctx }]);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.startDeletion"]);
  });

  test("confirming runs the auth confirmation, then the social purge with the media detach inside its transaction, then, after its commit, the file deletion requests, then the auth purge, in that order", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const [imageA, imageB] = [randomUUID(), randomUUID()];
    const ada = h.account({ images: [imageA, imageB] });
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "Ada" });
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion", "social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "social.commit", "media.requestDeletion(2)", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    // The image rows go in the social purge's own transaction, and their files are asked for only once it has committed,
    // for exactly the rows it deleted: a transaction that does not commit has asked for nothing.
    expect(h.seenTx).toEqual([h.tx]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[imageA, imageB]]);
    expect(h.purgedProfiles.get(ada.userId)).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)).toEqual({ deletedAt: h.now(), purgedAt: h.now() });
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 40)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a refused confirmation purges nothing", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ images: [randomUUID()] });
    const refused = await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "not_ada" }).catch((err: unknown) => err);
    expect(refused).toBeInstanceOf(AuthError);
    expect((refused as AuthError).message).toBe("handle_mismatch");
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)).toEqual({ deletedAt: null, purgedAt: null });
    expect(h.images.get(ada.userId)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("a purge that fails after the confirmation is logged and the confirmation still succeeds; the account stays pending for the job", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ images: [randomUUID()] });
    h.failing.add(ada.userId);
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "ada" });
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion", "social.purgeProfile"]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)).toEqual({ deletedAt: h.now(), purgedAt: null });
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    const errors = h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 50);
    expect(errors).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(errors[0]!.userId).toBe(ada.userId);
    expect(errors[0]!.msg).toMatch(/purge/);
  });

  test("the purge is safe to repeat: a second run detaches nothing, requests no deletion, and leaves the purged row as it was", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), images: [randomUUID()] });
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    const first = { ...h.users.get(ada.userId)!, profilePurgedAt: h.purgedProfiles.get(ada.userId) };
    expect(first).toEqual({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), purgedAt: h.now(), profilePurgedAt: h.now() });
    h.calls.length = 0;
    h.advance(60_000);
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "social.commit", "media.requestDeletion(0)", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[expect.any(String)], []]);
    expect({ ...h.users.get(ada.userId)!, profilePurgedAt: h.purgedProfiles.get(ada.userId) }).toEqual(first);
  });

  test("a purge whose transaction fails at the commit has asked for no file: its rows are back, a report may keep them, and only the run that commits asks", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const [imageA, imageB] = [randomUUID(), randomUUID()];
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), images: [imageA, imageB] });
    h.failingCommit.add(ada.userId);
    await expect(purge(h.deps, ada.userId)).rejects.toThrow(/commit/);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "social.rollback"]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toBeNull();
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[imageA, imageB]]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
  });

  test("a request for files that fails after the commit is logged with the account and does not keep the purge from finishing: the media module still owes it", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), images: [randomUUID(), randomUUID()] });
    h.failingRequest.once = true;
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "social.commit", "media.requestDeletion(2)", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    const errors = h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 50);
    expect(errors).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(errors[0]!.userId).toBe(ada.userId);
    expect(errors[0]!.msg).toMatch(/files .* could not be requested/);
    // A rerun finds no row left, so nothing here asks again: the request is the media module's to repeat.
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("the purge job", () => {
  test("purges every pending account, counts the ones that failed, and finishes on the next round what failed once", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 120_000), images: [randomUUID()] });
    const bob = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    h.account();
    h.failing.add(ada.userId);

    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 1, terminated: 0, held: 0 });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toBeNull();
    expect(h.users.get(bob.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    // The failure is logged with the account, and the round with its counts.
    expect(h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 50).map((line) => line.userId)).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    expect(h.lines.filter((line) => line.purged !== undefined).map((line) => [line.purged, line.failed])).toEqual([[1, 1]]);

    h.advance(PURGE_INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 0 });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[], [expect.any(String)]]);
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([]);
    // A round with nothing to do reports zeros and logs nothing.
    h.lines.length = 0;
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 0, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 0 });
    expect(h.lines).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("3f: an account whose address is held for a report is counted as held, not purged, stays pending each round, and is purged once the hold ends", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    const bob = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 30_000) });
    h.held.add(ada.userId);
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 1 });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toBeNull();
    expect(h.users.get(bob.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    // Each round runs the purge again, which changes nothing, and counts the account as held again.
    h.advance(PURGE_INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 0, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 1 });
    // The record is sent, declined or seven days old: the next round overwrites the address.
    h.held.delete(ada.userId);
    h.advance(PURGE_INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 0 });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
  });

  test("3e: the round first takes down the terminations that are due, adds what failed to `failed`, and purges the deletions whatever happened there", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const bob = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    const taken: string[] = [];
    // The moderation module's step: it calls the auth module's take-down for each account due, and counts.
    h.deps.moderation = {
      takeDownDue: async (takeDown) => {
        h.calls.push("moderation.takeDownDue");
        const made = await takeDown("terminated-1", { decidedAt: new Date(T0 - 1), imagesSealed: false });
        if (made) taken.push("terminated-1");
        return { terminated: made ? 1 : 0, failed: 1 };
      },
      forgetAccount: async () => undefined,
      exportFor: async () => {
        throw new Error("not exercised by the purge");
      },
    };
    h.deps.auth = { ...h.deps.auth, takeDownTerminated: async () => true };
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 1, terminated: 1, held: 0 });
    expect(taken).toEqual(["terminated-1"]);
    expect(h.calls[0]).toBe("moderation.takeDownDue");
    expect(h.users.get(bob.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    // A step that throws as a whole is logged, and the person's own deletion is purged all the same.
    const carl = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 30_000) });
    h.deps.moderation = { ...h.deps.moderation, takeDownDue: async () => Promise.reject(new Error("the moderation module is down")) };
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 0 });
    expect(h.users.get(carl.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(h.lines.some((line) => line.level >= 50 && /terminations due/.test(String(line.msg)))).toBe(true);
  });

  test("runs every five minutes under the lock job:account-purge, and skips a round another instance holds", async () => {
    expect(PURGE_INTERVAL_MS).toBe(5 * 60_000);
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    const lock = new MemoryJobLock(() => Date.now());
    const job = createPurgeJob(h.deps, lock);
    await lock.acquire("job:account-purge", "other", 10_000);
    expect(await job.round()).toBe("skipped");
    expect(h.calls).toEqual([]);
    await lock.release("job:account-purge", "other");
    expect(await job.round()).toBe("ran");
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(await lock.acquire("job:account-purge", "other", 10_000)).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("the purge and the reports the account sent (3c design, section 7.10)", () => {
  /** The harness with the moderation module's interface for this one: the forgetting is logged with the other calls, and can be made to fail. */
  function withModeration() {
    const h = harness();
    const forgotten: string[] = [];
    const failing = new Set<string>();
    h.deps.moderation = {
      // 3e: no termination is due in these tests.
      takeDownDue: async () => ({ terminated: 0, failed: 0 }),
      forgetAccount: async (userId) => {
        h.calls.push("moderation.forgetAccount");
        if (failing.delete(userId)) throw new Error("the forgetting failed");
        forgotten.push(userId);
      },
      // The export's side of the interface is not exercised by the purge; test/account/export.test.ts covers it.
      exportFor: async () => {
        throw new Error("not exercised by the deletion");
      },
    };
    return { ...h, forgotten, failingForget: failing };
  }

  test("the reporter links are forgotten after the social purge has committed and before the account counts as purged", async () => {

    expect(h.forgotten).toEqual([ada.userId]);

  test("a forgetting that fails leaves the account pending, and the next run does every step again and finishes", async () => {

    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0, terminated: 0, held: 0 });
    expect(h.forgotten).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
  });

  test("the confirmation purges through the same steps: the owner's request answers once their reports are forgotten too", async () => {
    const h = withModeration();
    const ada = h.account();
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "ada" });
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion", "social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "social.commit", "media.requestDeletion(0)", "moderation.forgetAccount", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    expect(h.forgotten).toEqual([ada.userId]);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, posix, relative, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

/**
 * Module boundaries (1a spec section 2.2, 2a spec section 2.2, 3a design section 5, 3c design section 5). Paths are relative to apps/api/src
 * with forward slashes. The rules are plain functions so the tests below can prove each one catches
 * a deliberate violation.
 */
interface SourceFile {
  path: string;
  source: string;
}

const SRC_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../src", import.meta.url));
const SCHEMA_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../packages/db/src/schema", import.meta.url));

/** Schema files that define auth-schema objects or shared helpers; every other schema file is public. */
const NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES = new Set(["auth.ts", "helpers.ts", "index.ts"]);
const AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE = "auth.ts";
// The command lines open both pools: grant-role changes a role on the auth pool, and staff.js reads there the staff keys
// that audit-verify checks the record against.
const AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts", "index.ts", "cli/grant-role.ts", "cli/staff.ts"]);
const AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts"]);

/** Modules that may only be entered through their index file. */
const MODULES = ["auth", "social", "media", "account", "staff", "moderation"] as const;

function walk(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return walk(full);
    return entry.name.endsWith(".ts") ? [full] : [];
  });
}

function loadSources(): SourceFile[] {
  return walk(SRC_ROOT).map((full) => ({ path: relative(SRC_ROOT, full).split(sep).join("/"), source: readFileSync(full, "utf8") }));
}

function exportedNames(file: string): string[] {
  const source = readFileSync(join(SCHEMA_ROOT, file), "utf8");
  return [...source.matchAll(/^export (?:const|function|type|interface|enum) ([A-Za-z0-9_]+)/gm)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Names exported by the public-schema files of @korbat/db (tables and enums the auth module must not touch). */
function publicSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  const names = new Set<string>();
  for (const file of readdirSync(SCHEMA_ROOT)) {
    if (!file.endsWith(".ts") || NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES.has(file)) continue;
    for (const name of exportedNames(file)) names.add(name);
  }
  return names;
}

/** Names exported by the auth-schema file of @korbat/db (tables and enums the social module must not touch). */
function authSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  return new Set(exportedNames(AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE));
}

/** Every module specifier in static imports, re-exports, side-effect imports and dynamic imports. */
function specifiers(source: string): string[] {
  return [...source.matchAll(/(?:\bfrom\s+|\bimport\s*\(\s*|\bimport\s+)["']([^"']+)["']/g)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Named bindings of every `import { ... } from "@korbat/db"`; a namespace import yields the marker "*". */
function dbImports(source: string): string[] {
  const names: string[] = [];
  for (const match of source.matchAll(/\bimport\s+(type\s+)?(\*\s+as\s+\w+|\{[^}]*\})\s+from\s+["'](@korbat\/db(?:\/[^"']*)?)["']/g)) {
    const bindings = match[2]!;
    if (bindings.startsWith("*")) {
      names.push("*");
      continue;
    }
    for (const part of bindings.slice(1, -1).split(",")) {
      const name = part.trim().replace(/^type\s+/, "").split(/\s+as\s+/)[0]!.trim();
      if (name) names.push(name);
    }
  }
  return names;
}

const insideAuth = (path: string) => path.startsWith("auth/");
const insideSocial = (path: string) => path.startsWith("social/");
const insideMedia = (path: string) => path.startsWith("media/");
const insideAccount = (path: string) => path.startsWith("account/");
const insideStaff = (path: string) => path.startsWith("staff/");
const insideModeration = (path: string) => path.startsWith("moderation/");

function findViolations(files: SourceFile[], publicNames: Set<string>, authNames: Set<string>): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;
      const target = posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/\.ts$/, "");
      for (const module of MODULES) {
        if (path.startsWith(`${module}/`)) continue;
        if (target.startsWith(`${module}/`) && target !== `${module}/index`) {
          violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is inside the ${module} module (use ./${module})`);
        }
      }
    }
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(DATABASE_URL_AUTH|authDb)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references the auth database pool`);
    }
    // Each encryption key with the list of the keys it replaced: after a rotation those still open what was stored before it.
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(TOTP_ENC_KEY|TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS|NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY|NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|IP_HASH_KEY)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references an auth key`);
    }
    if (insideAuth(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import auth-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    if (!insideMedia(path) && /\b(postMedia|post_media)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references post_media, which only the media module may touch`);
    }
    // The staff module (role korbat_api) reads and writes the public audit log; staff keys, staff sessions and enrolments
    // are credentials, the auth module's alone (3a design, section 5). The moderation module owns the moderation tables on
    // the same role: a notifier's contact and the staff links live in the auth schema, out of its reach (3c design, section 5).
    if (insideSocial(path) || insideMedia(path) || insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import public-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    // The account module sequences the other three through their index files and holds no table access of its own
    // (1b spec, section 5): no table or enum of either schema may be named in it. Db and DbTx, which are not schema
    // names, stay allowed, since a transaction is passed through it.
    if (insideAccount(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
      }
    }
    // The staff module uses the auth module's interface as the other modules do, never its repository or its session
    // store, which would hand it the auth tables; the moderation module likewise. Any mention counts, so a renamed,
    // namespace or dynamic import is caught as surely as a named one.
    if (insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      const module = insideStaff(path) ? "staff" : "moderation";
      for (const name of new Set([...source.matchAll(/\b(createAuthRepo|createSessions)\b/g)].map((m) => m[1]!))) {
        violations.push(`${path}: uses the auth module's ${name} (the ${module} module goes through the auth module's interface)`);
      }
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

/**
 * The source pins of the freeze (3c design, sections 6.1 and 6.5). The freeze of the path for suspected child sexual abuse
 * material holds only while every path of a kind passes one gate, so who may name what is pinned here, beside the
 * database's own pins of who names the predicate there:
 *   - `post_frozen` is named only in the media repository and the moderation repository, and `frozen_for` nowhere in the
 *     API: no other file decides by itself what is frozen;
 *   - a delete of `post_media` is written only in the media repository, whose every delete the keep trigger judges and
 *     whose every answer names only rows that are gone;
 *   - `requestDeletion` (asking the worker to delete an image's files) and `openImage` (opening an image file of the
 *     store) are named in a pinned list of files, each a pinned number of times, comments included: a new caller of
 *     either fails the test until whoever adds it has checked it against the gates and listed it.
 */
const POST_FROZEN_ALLOWED = new Set(["media/repo.ts", "moderation/repo.ts"]);
const POST_MEDIA_DELETE_ALLOWED = new Set(["media/repo.ts"]);
const POST_MEDIA_DELETE = /\bdelete\s+from\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:"?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?post_media\b|\btruncate\b[^;`]*\bpost_media\b|\.delete\(\s*postMedia\b/i;

function findFreezeViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    if (/\bfrozen_for\b/.test(source)) violations.push(`${path}: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name`);
    if (/\bpost_frozen\b/.test(source) && !POST_FROZEN_ALLOWED.has(path)) violations.push(`${path}: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may`);
    if (POST_MEDIA_DELETE.test(source) && !POST_MEDIA_DELETE_ALLOWED.has(path)) violations.push(`${path}: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may`);
  }
  return violations;
}

/** Every file that names `name` as a whole word, with how often, comments included. */
function mentions(files: SourceFile[], name: string): Record<string, number> {
  const found: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    // Cut at every word boundary: a whole word is then a piece of its own.
    const count = source.split(/\b/).filter((piece) => piece === name).length;
    if (count > 0) found[path] = count;
  }
  return found;
}

/**
 * Where `requestDeletion` is named. A deletion request names an id that a delete of post_media answered, an upload that
 * failed before it could be put on a post, or a file that has no row: the files module writes the request; the upload's
 * removal, the sweeper, the author's deletion (after its commit), the account's purge (after its commit) and the
 * disposal's caller (after its commit) ask for it through the module's interfaces; and the one retry of what the purge
 * and the disposal owe asks for it only for a row that is gone.
 */
const REQUEST_DELETION = {
  "account/flows/deletion.ts": 1,
  "media/cases.ts": 4,
  "media/context.ts": 2,
  "media/files.ts": 1,
  "media/flows/remove.ts": 1,
  "media/index.ts": 5,
  // The retry of owed deletions, which asks only for ids whose row it found gone.
  "media/owed.ts": 1,
  "media/sweeper.ts": 2,
  // The retention job, which asks for a batch's files after the commit of the transaction that deleted their rows.
  "moderation/retention.ts": 1,
  "social/context.ts": 1,
  "social/flows/posts.ts": 1,
};

/**
 * Where `openImage` is named: the files module, which opens a file of the store under its checks, and its three callers,
 * each behind its own reader's rule: serve (gate S), the export's open (which reads the row again) and the staff's image
 * (gate V).
 */
const OPEN_IMAGE = {
  "media/cases.ts": 1,
  "media/files.ts": 1,
  "media/flows/serve.ts": 1,
  "media/index.ts": 1,
};

describe("the freeze's source pins", () => {
  test("apps/api/src names post_frozen only in the two repositories, frozen_for nowhere, and deletes from post_media only in the media repository", () => {
    expect(findFreezeViolations(loadSources())).toEqual([]);
    // The media repository does name the predicate and does delete: the pins are about a file that exists.
    const repo = loadSources().find((file) => file.path === "media/repo.ts")!;
    expect(repo.source).toMatch(/\bpost_frozen\b/);
    expect(POST_MEDIA_DELETE.test(repo.source)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("catches the predicate named outside the two repositories, and its core named anywhere", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "sql`select public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen from post_media m`" },
      { path: "moderation/repo.ts", source: "sql`select not public.post_frozen(${postId}::uuid) as images_allowed`" },
      { path: "moderation/cases.ts", source: "const [row] = await tx.execute(sql`select public.post_frozen(${postId}::uuid) as frozen`);" },
      { path: "media/flows/serve.ts", source: "const frozen = await db.execute(sql`select post_frozen(${postId})`);" },
      { path: "staff/cases.ts", source: "await db.execute(sql`select public.frozen_for(${postId}::uuid, ${authorId}::uuid)`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "sql`select public.frozen_for(m.post_id, m.owner_id) from post_media m`" },
      // Another word that only contains the name is not the name.
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const post_frozen_label = 1; const unfrozen_for_now = 2;" },
    ];
    expect(findFreezeViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "moderation/cases.ts: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may",
      "media/flows/serve.ts: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may",
      "staff/cases.ts: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name",
      "media/repo.ts: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a delete of post_media outside the media repository, in SQL and through the query builder", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "await tx.execute(sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`);\nawait db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));" },
      { path: "media/sweeper.ts", source: "await db.execute(sql`delete from post_media where post_id is null and created_at < ${before}`);" },
      { path: "media/flows/remove.ts", source: "await deps.db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));" },
      { path: "media/cases.ts", source: 'await tx.execute(sql`DELETE FROM "public"."post_media" WHERE "id" = ${id}`);' },
      { path: "media/index.ts", source: "await tx.execute(sql`truncate table post_media cascade`);" },
      // Reading and updating image rows, and deleting something else, is not a delete of image rows.
      { path: "media/flows/status.ts", source: "await db.update(postMedia).set({ status }).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));\nawait db.delete(posts).where(eq(posts.id, id));\nconst rows = await db.execute(sql`select id from post_media`);" },
    ];
    expect(findFreezeViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "media/sweeper.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/flows/remove.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/cases.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/index.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
    ]);
  });

  test("requestDeletion and openImage are named in exactly the pinned files, each the pinned number of times", () => {
    expect(mentions(loadSources(), "requestDeletion")).toEqual(REQUEST_DELETION);
    expect(mentions(loadSources(), "openImage")).toEqual(OPEN_IMAGE);
  });

  test("catches a new caller of either, in a file of the list and in one outside it", () => {
    const real = loadSources();
    // A second request in the purge's flow, and a first one in a file that had none.
    const withCallers = real
      .map((file) => (file.path === "account/flows/deletion.ts" ? { ...file, source: `${file.source}\nawait deps.media.requestDeletion(kept);` } : file))
      .concat([{ path: "moderation/decide.ts", source: "await deps.media.requestDeletion(ids);" }]);
    expect(mentions(withCallers, "requestDeletion")).not.toEqual(REQUEST_DELETION);
    expect(mentions(withCallers, "requestDeletion")).toMatchObject({ "account/flows/deletion.ts": 2, "moderation/decide.ts": 1 });
    // A fourth opener of the store's files.
    const withOpener = real.concat([{ path: "staff/cases.ts", source: 'const file = await files.openImage(id, "large");' }]);
    expect(mentions(withOpener, "openImage")).not.toEqual(OPEN_IMAGE);
    // A name that only contains the word is not counted.
    expect(mentions([{ path: "x.ts", source: "requestDeletions(); reopenImage(); openImages();" }], "requestDeletion")).toEqual({});
    expect(mentions([{ path: "x.ts", source: "requestDeletions(); reopenImage(); openImages();" }], "openImage")).toEqual({});
  });
});

/**
 * The source pins of account sanctions (3e design, sections 11 and 12.2; invariant 23): no write of an account is added
 * without the one predicate.
 *   - The predicate's three fragments, exported by lib/standing.ts (`liveNotSuspended`, and the two halves that a locking
 *     statement answers separately, `suspendedAt` and `reportsRestrictedAt`), are named in a pinned list of files, each a
 *     pinned number of times, comments included, as REQUEST_DELETION is: whoever adds a write on behalf of an account adds
 *     its site to the list, and the auth module never names one. So is the closing judgment (`closingJudgment`, 3e's
 *     review), the last statement of a write's transaction, which reads both halves.
 *   - The profile's three derived columns are named in apps/api/src only in lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts's
 *     lockAccounts and the moderation module's standing-repo.ts, in SQL or by drizzle's names: no other file decides by
 *     itself whether an account is suspended. Their one writer is the database's standing_apply (the function pin of 6.6).
 */
const STANDING_PREDICATE = {
  // social/repo.ts, 3e Task 6: Explore's round applies the predicate to the candidates' authors and to the engagers at the
  // round's time, and the page and the chip to the authors at the read's (explorePage, listedInExplore).
  liveNotSuspended: { "lib/standing.ts": 1, "media/repo.ts": 2, "profiles/store.ts": 3, "social/repo.ts": 6 },
  // social/repo.ts, 3e Task 6: the author's Explore status reads whether the author is suspended (exploreFacts). lib/standing.ts,
  // 3e's review: the closing judgment reads both halves.
  suspendedAt: { "lib/standing.ts": 3, "social/repo.ts": 7 },
  reportsRestrictedAt: { "lib/standing.ts": 2, "social/repo.ts": 2 },
  // 3e's review (database1): the writes that end with the closing judgment: the social repository's (judgeActing), the
  // upload's row, and the intake of a report under a rule. The profile store's badge and the profile's edit end with
  // their UPDATE, made once the row is held.
  closingJudgment: { "lib/standing.ts": 1, "media/repo.ts": 2, "moderation/intake.ts": 2, "social/repo.ts": 2 },
};
const STANDING_COLUMNS_ALLOWED = new Set(["lib/standing.ts", "social/repo.ts", "moderation/standing-repo.ts"]);
const STANDING_COLUMNS = ["suspended_from", "suspended_until", "reports_restricted_until", "suspendedFrom", "suspendedUntil", "reportsRestrictedUntil"];
/** Whether a file names one of the derived columns as a whole word, by the same cut as `mentions`. */
const namesStandingColumn = (file: SourceFile): boolean => STANDING_COLUMNS.some((name) => mentions([file], name)[file.path] !== undefined);

function findStandingViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  return files.filter((file) => namesStandingColumn(file) && !STANDING_COLUMNS_ALLOWED.has(file.path)).map(({ path }) => `${path}: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may`);
}

describe("the source pins of account sanctions (3e)", () => {
  test("the predicate's fragments are named in exactly the pinned files, each the pinned number of times; the auth module names none", () => {
    for (const [name, pinned] of Object.entries(STANDING_PREDICATE)) expect(mentions(loadSources(), name), name).toEqual(pinned);
    // The auth module names none: no file of it is in any of the pinned lists.
    for (const pinned of Object.values(STANDING_PREDICATE)) expect(Object.keys(pinned).filter((path) => path.startsWith("auth/"))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches a new write that names the predicate, in a pinned file and in one outside the list", () => {
    const real = loadSources();
    const withWrites = real
      .map((file) => (file.path === "media/repo.ts" ? { ...file, source: file.source + String.fromCharCode(10) + 'sql`update post_media set alt = null where ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)}`;' } : file))
      .concat([{ path: "moderation/texts.ts", source: 'await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from profiles p where ${suspendedAt("p", WRITE_CLOCK)}`);' }]);
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "liveNotSuspended")).not.toEqual(STANDING_PREDICATE.liveNotSuspended);
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "liveNotSuspended")).toMatchObject({ "media/repo.ts": 3 });
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "suspendedAt")).toMatchObject({ "moderation/texts.ts": 1 });
    expect(mentions(withWrites, "suspendedAt")).not.toEqual(STANDING_PREDICATE.suspendedAt);
  });

  test("the three derived columns are named only in lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts, and lib/standing.ts does name them", () => {
    expect(findStandingViolations(loadSources())).toEqual([]);
    expect(namesStandingColumn(loadSources().find((file) => file.path === "lib/standing.ts")!)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("catches a derived column named elsewhere, in SQL and by drizzle's name", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "lib/standing.ts", source: "sql`(${p}.suspended_from is not null and ${p}.suspended_from <= ${at} and ${at} < ${p}.suspended_until)`" },
      { path: "moderation/standing-repo.ts", source: "sql`select reports_restricted_until from profiles`" },
      { path: "social/flows/posts.ts", source: "const [row] = await db.execute(sql`select suspended_until from profiles where id = ${viewer}::uuid`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "await db.select({ until: profiles.suspendedUntil }).from(profiles);" },
      { path: "auth/flows/badge.ts", source: "if (profile.reportsRestrictedUntil) return;" },
      // A word that only contains the name is not the name.
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const unsuspended_from_now = 1;" },
    ];
    expect(findStandingViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "social/flows/posts.ts: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may",
      "media/repo.ts: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may",
      "auth/flows/badge.ts: names a derived column of an account's standing, which only lib/standing.ts, social/repo.ts and moderation/standing-repo.ts may",
    ]);
  });
});

/**
 * The watcher's boundary (3f design, section 5): notify, an entry point of its own (dist/notify.js), imports the contracts,
 * the database package and Node's and its packages' modules, and nothing of the API's: no relative import leaves
 * src/notify. Nothing outside it imports it either: the API holds no mailbox credential, no ntfy token and no route to the
 * push network, and the watcher shares no code with the API that could carry one in.
 */
function findNotifyViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    const inside = path.startsWith("notify/");
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;
      const target = posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec));
      if (inside && !target.startsWith("notify/")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, outside the watcher`);
      if (!inside && target.startsWith("notify/")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, inside the watcher`);
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the watcher's boundary (3f)", () => {
  test("src/notify imports nothing of the API's modules, and nothing imports src/notify", () => {
    const files = loadSources();
    expect(files.filter((file) => file.path.startsWith("notify/")).map((file) => file.path).sort()).toEqual(["notify/imap.ts", "notify/main.ts", "notify/push.ts"]);
    expect(findNotifyViolations(files)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches an import of an API module from the watcher, and an import of the watcher from the API", () => {
    expect(
      findNotifyViolations([
        { path: "notify/main.ts", source: 'import { loadConfig } from "../config"; import { publish } from "./push";' },
        { path: "notify/push.ts", source: 'import { staffAlert } from "../moderation";' },
        { path: "moderation/alerts.ts", source: 'import { TOPICS } from "../notify/push";' },
        { path: "index.ts", source: 'import { ALERT_KINDS } from "@korbat/contracts";' },
      ]),
    ).toEqual(["notify/main.ts: imports ../config, outside the watcher", "notify/push.ts: imports ../moderation, outside the watcher", "moderation/alerts.ts: imports ../notify/push, inside the watcher"]);
  });
});

/**
 * The hand-over's boundary (3f design, section 5 and invariant 16): handover.ts, an entry point of its own
 * (dist/handover.js), imports nothing under ./ (no module of the API, so no database, no configuration and no copy of
 * anything that could reach either) and only Node's own modules, none of which opens a socket or a process; nothing
 * imports it. And no file outside media/ but config.ts and index.ts names the store's directory setting, MEDIA_STORE_DIR:
 * the store is read through the media module, or by the hand-over's program under its fixed mount.
 */
const SOCKET_MODULES = new Set(["node:net", "node:http", "node:https", "node:http2", "node:dgram", "node:tls", "node:child_process", "node:worker_threads", "node:cluster"]);
function findHandoverViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (path === "handover.ts") {
        if (spec.startsWith(".")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, a module of the API`);
        else if (!spec.startsWith("node:")) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is not one of Node's own modules`);
        else if (SOCKET_MODULES.has(spec)) violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which can open a socket or a process`);
      } else if (spec.startsWith(".") && posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/[.]ts$/, "") === "handover") {
        violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, the hand-over's program`);
      }
    }
    if (/MEDIA_STORE_DIR/.test(source) && !path.startsWith("media/") && path !== "config.ts" && path !== "index.ts") {
      violations.push(`${path}: names MEDIA_STORE_DIR, which only the media module, config.ts and index.ts may`);
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the hand-over's boundary (3f Task 5)", () => {
  test("handover.ts imports only Node's own modules and none that opens a socket, nothing imports it, and no file outside media/ but config.ts and index.ts names the store's directory setting", () => {
    const files = loadSources();
    expect(files.map((file) => file.path)).toContain("handover.ts");
    expect(findHandoverViolations(files)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches an import of an API module or a package from the hand-over, a socket's module, an import of the hand-over, and the store's setting named elsewhere", () => {
    expect(
      findHandoverViolations([
        { path: "handover.ts", source: 'import { storedImageName } from "./media"; import { sql } from "drizzle-orm"; import { connect } from "node:net"; import { crc32 } from "node:zlib";' },
        { path: "cli/records.ts", source: 'import { zipStored } from "../handover";' },
        { path: "cli/staff.ts", source: "const dir = env.MEDIA_STORE_DIR;" },
        { path: "media/files.ts", source: "const dir = config.MEDIA_STORE_DIR;" },
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      "handover.ts: imports ./media, a module of the API",
      "handover.ts: imports drizzle-orm, which is not one of Node's own modules",
      "handover.ts: imports node:net, which can open a socket or a process",
      "cli/records.ts: imports ../handover, the hand-over's program",
      "cli/staff.ts: names MEDIA_STORE_DIR, which only the media module, config.ts and index.ts may",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("module boundaries", () => {
  test("walks the real source tree", () => {
    const paths = loadSources().map((f) => f.path);
    expect(paths).toContain("auth/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("social/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("media/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("account/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("staff/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("moderation/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("cli/staff.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("app.ts");
    expect(publicSchemaNames()).toContain("profiles");
    expect(publicSchemaNames()).not.toContain("users");
    expect(authSchemaNames()).toContain("users");
    expect(authSchemaNames()).not.toContain("posts");
  });

  test("apps/api/src has no boundary violations", () => {
    expect(findViolations(loadSources(), publicSchemaNames(), authSchemaNames())).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("allows the module indexes, the permitted pool owners and each module's own schema", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createAuth } from "./auth";\nimport type { Auth } from "./auth/index";\nimport { createSocial } from "./social";` },
      { path: "profiles/store.ts", source: `import { isUniqueViolation } from "../auth";` },
      { path: "cli/grant-role.ts", source: `const authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `const authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "config.ts", source: `AUTH_HMAC_KEY: base64Key, IP_HASH_KEY: base64Key, TOTP_ENC_KEY: versionedKey, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: url` },
      { path: "auth/repo.ts", source: `import { users, sessions, type Db } from "@korbat/db";\nconst k = config.TOTP_ENC_KEY;` },
      { path: "social/repo.ts", source: `import { posts, profiles, type Db } from "@korbat/db";\nimport { SocialError } from "./context";` },
      { path: "social/routes.ts", source: `import type { Auth } from "../auth";` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `import { createAccount } from "./account";\nimport { createMedia } from "./media";` },
      { path: "account/routes.ts", source: `import type { AuthForAccount } from "../auth";\nimport type { SocialForAccount } from "../social";\nimport { buildExport } from "./flows/export";` },
      { path: "account/flows/deletion.ts", source: `import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";\nimport type { MediaForAccount } from "../../media";` },
      { path: "cli/staff.ts", source: `import { createStaff } from "../staff";\nconst authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "staff/audit.ts", source: `import { auditHead, auditLog, profiles, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "staff/routes.ts", source: `import { AuthError, type Auth } from "../auth";\nimport { staffGate } from "./gate";` },
      { path: "staff/cases.ts", source: `import { ModerationError, type ModerationForStaff } from "../moderation";` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `import { createModeration } from "./moderation";\nimport { socialForModeration } from "./social";` },
      { path: "moderation/repo.ts", source: `import { cases, decisions, evidenceSnapshots, intakes, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";\nimport { ModerationError } from "./context";` },
      { path: "moderation/decide.ts", source: `import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";\nimport { boundLockWaits } from "../lib/lock-bounds";\nimport type { SocialForModeration } from "../social";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["profiles", "posts", "auditLog", "auditHead", "cases", "decisions", "evidenceSnapshots", "intakes"]), new Set(["users", "sessions"]))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the auth module", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "routes/posts.ts", source: `import { hashPassword } from "../auth/passwords";` },
      { path: "app.ts", source: `export { createSessions } from "./auth/sessions.ts";\nconst m = await import("./auth/repo");` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "routes/posts.ts: imports ../auth/passwords, which is inside the auth module (use ./auth)",
      "app.ts: imports ./auth/sessions.ts, which is inside the auth module (use ./auth)",
      "app.ts: imports ./auth/repo, which is inside the auth module (use ./auth)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the social module, from outside it and from the auth module", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createSocialRepo } from "./social/repo";` },
      { path: "auth/flows/signup.ts", source: `import { createPost } from "../../social/flows/posts";` },
      { path: "social/flows/graph.ts", source: `import { ownProfile } from "./posts";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./social/repo, which is inside the social module (use ./social)",
      "auth/flows/signup.ts: imports ../../social/flows/posts, which is inside the social module (use ./social)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the media module, post_media outside it, and the auth schema inside it", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createMediaRepo } from "./media/repo";\nimport { createMedia } from "./media";` },
      { path: "social/repo.ts", source: `import { postMedia, posts } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const rows = await db.execute(sql`select * from post_media`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: `import { postMedia, posts, users, type Db } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "media/flows/serve.ts", source: `import type { MediaDeps } from "../context";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["posts", "postMedia"]), new Set(["users"]))).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./media/repo, which is inside the media module (use ./media)",
      "social/repo.ts: references post_media, which only the media module may touch",
      "social/views.ts: references post_media, which only the media module may touch",
      "media/repo.ts: imports auth-schema users from @korbat/db",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the account module, and a table or enum of either schema inside it", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createZipWriter } from "./account/zip";\nimport { createAccount } from "./account";` },
      { path: "social/flows/graph.ts", source: `import { buildExport } from "../../account/flows/export";` },
      { path: "account/flows/export.ts", source: `import { posts, users, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "account/purge.ts", source: `import * as db from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "account/zip.ts", source: `import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["posts"]), new Set(["users"]))).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./account/zip, which is inside the account module (use ./account)",
      "social/flows/graph.ts: imports ../../account/flows/export, which is inside the account module (use ./account)",
      "account/flows/export.ts: imports public-schema posts from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)",
      "account/flows/export.ts: imports auth-schema users from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)",
      "account/purge.ts: namespace import of @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches auth pool and auth key references outside their owners", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "routes/posts.ts", source: `const url = config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH;` },
      { path: "profiles/store.ts", source: `export function f(authDb: Db) {}` },
      { path: "lib/hash.ts", source: `const key = config.IP_HASH_KEY;` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `const k = config.AUTH_HMAC_KEY;` },
      // The key a notifier's name and address are encrypted under is the auth module's too: the moderation module, which
      // names contacts by their ids, never sees it.
```

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { Platform } from "@korbat/contracts";
import pino from "pino";
import type { AuthConfig, AuthDeps, RequestContext } from "../../src/auth/context";
import { parseVersionedKey, randomToken, sha256Hex } from "../../src/auth/crypto";
import { MemoryKv } from "../../src/auth/kv";
import { createLockout } from "../../src/auth/lockout";
import type {
  ActiveSessionRow,
  AddPasskeyOutcome,
  AuthEventType,
  AuthRepo,
  DeviceRow,
  EmailCodeRow,
  LockDownInput,
  LockDownOutcome,
  NewPasskey,
  PasskeyLimits,
  PasskeyListRow,
  PasskeyRow,
  SessionListRow,
  UserRow,
} from "../../src/auth/repo";
import { createSessions, SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MS, SESSION_IDLE_MS, type Factors, type Session } from "../../src/auth/sessions";
import { devProvider } from "../../src/auth/verify/dev";
import { MemoryMailer } from "../../src/mail/memory";

export interface RecordedEvent {
  userId: string | null;
  type: AuthEventType;
  deviceId: string | null;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export const TEST_TERMS = "draft-test";

/**
 * A session of a user, as the deletion and lockdown flows revoke it and, since Task 5, as the sign-in and re-authentication
 * flows issue, resolve and rotate it. The first three fields are all those older flows read; the rest let findActiveSession
 * answer a full row.
 */
export interface RecordedSession {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  revokedAt: Date | null;
  deviceId: string;
  handle: string;
  factors: Record<string, number>;
  passkeyId: string | null;
  reauthAt: Date;
  createdAt: Date;
  lastUsedAt: Date;
  expiresAt: Date;
  absoluteExpiresAt: Date;
}

export interface RecordedDevice {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  revokedAt: Date | null;
  /** What the passkey flows read of the row: the platform for a passkey's default name and the label for the Security list. */
  platform: Platform;
  label: string | null;
  /** The keyed hash a sign-in looks a device up by; absent on the devices h.session and h.user seed, which no lookup finds. */
  deviceHash?: string;
}

/** A passkey of a user, as the registration writes it and the lockdown and the management flows read it. */
export type RecordedPasskey = PasskeyRow;

/**
 * The auth flows without a database: users, email codes, sessions, devices and passkeys live in memory, and the
 * repository fake holds only the methods the email-change (with its undo link), badge, deletion, not-me,
 * lockdown and TOTP confirmation flows call (and the lookups the sign-in starts make), checked against the real signatures. The key-value store and the
 * mailer are the in-memory ones; the clock moves only when a test says so, so expiries and timestamps
 * compare exactly; and events are kept as the server would write them to auth_events. The integration
 * harness (test/integration/flow-harness.ts) runs flows against the real repository instead.
 */
export function memoryFlowHarness(start = 1_789_000_000_000) {
  let t = start;
  const now = () => new Date(t);
  const users = new Map<string, UserRow>();
  const codes: EmailCodeRow[] = [];
  const events: RecordedEvent[] = [];
  const sessions: RecordedSession[] = [];
  const devices: RecordedDevice[] = [];
  const passkeys: RecordedPasskey[] = [];
  /**
   * When each event was recorded, at the harness clock, kept beside the events rather than on them: the tests compare
   * the events with the exact objects the flows write, and the daily passkey bound is the only reader of the times.
   */
  const eventTimes = new WeakMap<RecordedEvent, number>();
  const recordEvent = (event: RecordedEvent) => {
    events.push(event);
    eventTimes.set(event, t);
  };
  /** The handle of each account's profile, which the deletion flow compares the typed handle with. */
  const handles = new Map<string, string>();
  /** Repository methods told to fail: "takeDown" and "lockDown" each fail as a transaction that breaks off midway, after staging its writes and before any lands. */
  const faults = new Set<"takeDown" | "lockDown">();
  /** A device as the real row reads, from what the harness keeps of it; the hash and the times are placeholders no flow reads here. */
  const deviceRow = (device: RecordedDevice): DeviceRow => ({
    id: device.id,
    userId: device.userId,
    deviceHash: device.deviceHash ?? `hash-${device.id}`,
    label: device.label,
    platform: device.platform,
    firstSeenAt: now(),
    lastSeenAt: now(),
    ipHash: null,
    revokedAt: device.revokedAt,
  });
  /** A passkey with the label of the device that added it, as the real join answers it: null once that device is gone. */
  const withDevice = (passkey: RecordedPasskey): PasskeyListRow => ({ ...passkey, createdOn: devices.find((d) => d.id === passkey.createdDeviceId)?.label ?? null });
  /**
   * The daily bound's reading, as the real statement makes it: the times of the account's latest passkey_added events within
   * the window, at most `limit` of them, and the seconds until the oldest of those leaves the window.
   */
  const recentPasskeyAdditions = (userId: string, withinMs: number, limit: number) => {
    const recent = events
      .filter((e) => e.userId === userId && e.type === "passkey_added")
      .map((e) => eventTimes.get(e)!)
      .filter((at) => at > t - withinMs)
      .sort((a, b) => b - a)
      .slice(0, limit);
    const oldest = recent.at(-1);
    return { count: recent.length, retryAfterSeconds: oldest === undefined ? 0 : Math.ceil((oldest + withinMs - t) / 1000) };
  };
  /**
   * Step 1's rows for a user, as the real repository's takeDownRows writes them: live sessions revoked (their ids
   * returned), devices, codes and passkeys gone, and the WebAuthn user handle cleared (1c design, section 7.7).
   */
  const takeDownRows = (userId: string, at: Date): string[] => {
    const live = sessions.filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null);
    for (const s of live) s.revokedAt = at;
    for (let i = devices.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (devices[i]!.userId === userId) devices.splice(i, 1);
    for (let i = codes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (codes[i]!.userId === userId) codes.splice(i, 1);
    for (let i = passkeys.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (passkeys[i]!.userId === userId) passkeys.splice(i, 1);
    const row = users.get(userId);
    if (row) row.webauthnUserId = null;
    return live.map((s) => s.id);
  };
  const repo = {
    async findUserById(id: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      const row = users.get(id);
      return row && row.deletedAt === null ? { ...row } : undefined;
    },
    async findUserByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      // As the real lookup: the address in any case, and never a deleted row.
      const row = [...users.values()].find((u) => u.email.toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase());
      return row && row.deletedAt === null ? { ...row } : undefined;
    },
    async setPasswordFailures(userId: string, failedLogins: number, lockedUntil: Date | null): Promise<void> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) {
        row.failedLogins = failedLogins;
        row.lockedUntil = lockedUntil;
      }
    },
    async createEmailCode(input: Parameters<AuthRepo["createEmailCode"]>[0]): Promise<void> {
      codes.push({ id: randomUUID(), ...input, attempts: 0, consumedAt: null, createdAt: now() });
    },
    async findEmailCode(flowId: string): Promise<EmailCodeRow | undefined> {
      const row = codes.find((c) => c.flowId === flowId);
      return row ? { ...row } : undefined;
    },
    async addCodeAttempt(id: string): Promise<number> {
      const row = codes.find((c) => c.id === id);
      if (!row) return Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
      row.attempts += 1;
      return row.attempts;
    },
    async consumeEmailCode(id: string, at: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      const row = codes.find((c) => c.id === id);
      if (!row || row.consumedAt !== null) return false;
      row.consumedAt = at;
      return true;
    },
    async changeEmail(userId: string, email: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      // As the real unique index on lower(email), deleted rows included: the driver error that the flow recognises through isUniqueViolation.
      for (const other of users.values()) {
        if (other.id !== userId && other.email.toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase()) {
          throw Object.assign(new Error('duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_lower_idx"'), { code: "23505" });
        }
      }
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row) return;
      row.email = email;
      row.emailVerifiedAt = at;
    },
    async setPasswordHash(userId: string, passwordHash: string | null, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      // As the real statement: setting or clearing a password also clears any lockout, and records when.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) Object.assign(row, { passwordHash, passwordChangedAt: at, failedLogins: 0, lockedUntil: null });
    },
    async enableTotp(userId: string, input: { secretEnc: string; recoveryCodesHash: string[]; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      // As the real statement: unconditional, whatever the row held, and the last accepted step starts over.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) Object.assign(row, { totpSecretEnc: input.secretEnc, totpEnabledAt: input.now, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: input.recoveryCodesHash });
    },
    async disableTotp(userId: string): Promise<void> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) Object.assign(row, { totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] });
    },
    async lockDown(userId: string, input: LockDownInput): Promise<LockDownOutcome> {
      // One transaction, as the real one: when it fails midway nothing it would have written lands.
      if (faults.has("lockDown")) throw new Error("the lockdown transaction failed midway and was rolled back");
      const live = sessions.filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null);
      for (const s of live) s.revokedAt = input.now;
      for (const device of devices) if (device.userId === userId && device.revokedAt === null) device.revokedAt = input.now;
      // As the real statement: the user's passkeys created at or after `since`, plus any of theirs the caller names.
      const passkeysRemoved: string[] = [];
      for (let i = passkeys.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        const passkey = passkeys[i]!;
        if (passkey.userId !== userId) continue;
        if (passkey.createdAt.getTime() >= input.since.getTime() || input.passkeyIds.includes(passkey.id)) {
          passkeysRemoved.push(passkey.id);
          passkeys.splice(i, 1);
        }
      }
      const row = users.get(userId);
      // As the real read of the locked row: an account that is gone has no two-factor to clear.
      const totpCleared = row !== undefined && row.deletedAt === null && row.totpEnabledAt !== null && row.totpEnabledAt.getTime() >= input.since.getTime();
      if (row) {
        // The password as setPasswordHash clears it, and two-factor as disableTotp turns it off.
        Object.assign(row, { passwordHash: null, passwordChangedAt: input.now, failedLogins: 0, lockedUntil: null });
        if (totpCleared) Object.assign(row, { totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] });
      }
      recordEvent({ userId, type: input.event.type, deviceId: input.event.deviceId, metadata: { ...input.event.metadata, passkeysRemoved, totpCleared, passwordCleared: true } });
      return { sessionIds: live.map((s) => s.id), passkeysRemoved, totpCleared };
    },
    async setPhoneHash(userId: string, phoneHash: string | null): Promise<void> {
      // As the real partial unique index on phone_hash, deleted rows included: the driver error that the flow recognises through isUniqueViolation.
      if (phoneHash !== null) {
        for (const other of users.values()) {
          if (other.id !== userId && other.phoneHash === phoneHash) {
            throw Object.assign(new Error('duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_phone_hash_idx"'), { code: "23505" });
          }
        }
      }
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) row.phoneHash = phoneHash;
    },
    async appendEvent(input: Parameters<AuthRepo["appendEvent"]>[0]): Promise<void> {
      recordEvent({ userId: input.userId, type: input.type, deviceId: input.deviceId ?? null, metadata: input.metadata ?? {} });
    },
    async findDeviceById(id: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const device = devices.find((d) => d.id === id);
      return device ? deviceRow(device) : undefined;
    },
    async ensureWebauthnUserId(userId: string, candidate: Buffer): Promise<Buffer | undefined> {
      // As the real compare-and-set: the first candidate sticks, every later call reads it back.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt !== null) return undefined;
      row.webauthnUserId ??= candidate;
      return row.webauthnUserId;
    },
    async countPasskeys(userId: string): Promise<number> {
      return passkeys.filter((p) => p.userId === userId).length;
    },
    async listPasskeys(userId: string): Promise<PasskeyListRow[]> {
      // Newest first, as the real statement orders them.
      return passkeys
        .filter((p) => p.userId === userId)
        .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.getTime() - a.createdAt.getTime())
        .map(withDevice);
    },
    async findPasskey(id: string, userId: string): Promise<PasskeyListRow | undefined> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id && p.userId === userId);
      return passkey ? withDevice(passkey) : undefined;
    },
    async recentPasskeyAdditions(userId: string, withinMs: number, limit: number): Promise<{ count: number; retryAfterSeconds: number }> {
      return recentPasskeyAdditions(userId, withinMs, limit);
    },
    async addPasskey(input: NewPasskey, limits: PasskeyLimits): Promise<AddPasskeyOutcome> {
      // As the real transaction: the account locked, both bounds checked again, then the row and its event, or nothing.
      const row = users.get(input.userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt !== null) return { ok: false, reason: "gone" };
      if (passkeys.filter((p) => p.userId === input.userId).length >= limits.passkeys) return { ok: false, reason: "cap" };
      const additions = recentPasskeyAdditions(input.userId, limits.windowMs, limits.additions);
      if (additions.count >= limits.additions) return { ok: false, reason: "daily", retryAfterSeconds: additions.retryAfterSeconds };
      // As the real unique index on credential_id: the driver error that the flow recognises through isUniqueViolation.
      if (passkeys.some((p) => p.credentialId === input.credentialId)) {
```
