```ts
      }
      const passkey: RecordedPasskey = { id: randomUUID(), lastUsedAt: null, suspectAt: null, ...input };
      passkeys.push(passkey);
      recordEvent({ userId: input.userId, type: "passkey_added", deviceId: input.createdDeviceId, metadata: { passkeyId: passkey.id } });
      return { ok: true, passkey: { ...passkey } };
    },
    async renamePasskey(id: string, userId: string, name: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id && p.userId === userId);
      if (!passkey) return false;
      passkey.name = name;
      return true;
    },
    async deletePasskey(id: string, userId: string): Promise<{ name: string } | undefined> {
      const index = passkeys.findIndex((p) => p.id === id && p.userId === userId);
      if (index === -1) return undefined;
      const [removed] = passkeys.splice(index, 1);
      return { name: removed!.name };
    },
    async findPasskeyByCredentialId(credentialId: string): Promise<PasskeyRow | undefined> {
      // As the real lookup: any account's, and the flow refuses a deleted owner through findUserById.
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.credentialId === credentialId);
      return passkey ? { ...passkey } : undefined;
    },
    async findPasskeyByCredential(credentialId: string, userId: string): Promise<PasskeyRow | undefined> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.credentialId === credentialId && p.userId === userId);
      return passkey ? { ...passkey } : undefined;
    },
    async claimPasskeyUse(id: string, newCounter: number, backedUp: boolean, at: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      // As the real conditional update: a suspect passkey never matches, and the counter must move forward unless both are zero.
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id);
      if (!passkey || passkey.suspectAt !== null) return false;
      if (!((newCounter === 0 && passkey.counter === 0) || newCounter > passkey.counter)) return false;
      passkey.counter = newCounter;
      passkey.lastUsedAt = at;
      passkey.backedUp = backedUp;
      return true;
    },
    async suspectPasskey(id: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id);
      if (passkey && passkey.suspectAt === null) passkey.suspectAt = at;
    },
    async findDevice(userId: string, deviceHashValue: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const device = devices.find((d) => d.userId === userId && d.deviceHash === deviceHashValue && d.revokedAt === null);
      return device ? deviceRow(device) : undefined;
    },
    async createDevice(input: { userId: string; deviceHash: string; label: string; platform: string; ipHash: string | null }): Promise<DeviceRow> {
      const device: RecordedDevice = { id: randomUUID(), userId: input.userId, revokedAt: null, platform: input.platform as Platform, label: input.label, deviceHash: input.deviceHash };
      devices.push(device);
      return deviceRow(device);
    },
    async touchDevice(): Promise<void> {
      // The row's last-seen and ip are placeholders no flow reads here, so touching it changes nothing observable.
    },
    async createSession(input: {
      id: string;
      userId: string;
      deviceId: string;
      now: Date;
      expiresAt: Date;
      absoluteExpiresAt: Date;
      factors?: Record<string, number>;
      passkeyId?: string | null;
    }): Promise<void> {
      // As the real insert: the reauth time is the latest of the factors, and a fresh handle stands in for the column's default.
      const factors = input.factors ?? {};
      const times = Object.values(factors);
      sessions.push({
        id: input.id,
        userId: input.userId,
        revokedAt: null,
        deviceId: input.deviceId,
        handle: randomUUID(),
        factors,
        passkeyId: input.passkeyId ?? null,
        reauthAt: times.length > 0 ? new Date(Math.max(...times)) : input.now,
        createdAt: input.now,
        lastUsedAt: input.now,
        expiresAt: input.expiresAt,
        absoluteExpiresAt: input.absoluteExpiresAt,
      });
    },
    async findActiveSession(id: string, at: Date): Promise<ActiveSessionRow | undefined> {
      // As the real joins: the session, its account and its device must all be live.
      const row = sessions.find((s) => s.id === id && s.revokedAt === null && s.expiresAt > at && s.absoluteExpiresAt > at);
      if (!row) return undefined;
      const user = users.get(row.userId);
      if (!user || user.deletedAt !== null) return undefined;
      const device = devices.find((d) => d.id === row.deviceId && d.revokedAt === null);
      if (!device) return undefined;
      return {
        id: row.id,
        userId: row.userId,
        deviceId: row.deviceId,
        role: user.role,
        onboardedAt: user.onboardedAt,
        totpEnabledAt: user.totpEnabledAt,
        reauthAt: row.reauthAt,
        lastUsedAt: row.lastUsedAt,
        expiresAt: row.expiresAt,
        absoluteExpiresAt: row.absoluteExpiresAt,
        handle: row.handle,
        factors: row.factors,
        passkeyId: row.passkeyId,
      };
    },
    async rotateSession(id: string, newId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      // As the real statement: the primary key changes in place for a live row, and everything else stays.
      const row = sessions.find((s) => s.id === id && s.revokedAt === null);
      if (!row) return false;
      row.id = newId;
      return true;
    },
    async writeFactor(id: string, kind: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      // As the real statement: the kind's time is set or replaced and the reauth time follows it.
      const row = sessions.find((s) => s.id === id);
      if (!row) return;
      row.factors = { ...row.factors, [kind]: at.getTime() };
      row.reauthAt = at;
    },
    async claimTotpStep(userId: string, step: number): Promise<boolean> {
      // As the real conditional update: a step no later than the last accepted one is refused, so a code cannot be reused.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || (row.totpLastStep !== null && row.totpLastStep >= step)) return false;
      row.totpLastStep = step;
      return true;
    },
    async revokeAllSessions(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const live = sessions.filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null);
      for (const s of live) s.revokedAt = at;
      return live.map((s) => s.id);
    },
    async listActiveSessions(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<SessionListRow[]> {
      // As the real statement: the user's sessions that are neither revoked nor expired, most recently used first, each with its device's label.
      return sessions
        .filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null && s.expiresAt > at && s.absoluteExpiresAt > at)
        .sort((a, b) => b.lastUsedAt.getTime() - a.lastUsedAt.getTime())
        .map((s) => {
          const device = devices.find((d) => d.id === s.deviceId);
          return { id: s.id, handle: s.handle, deviceLabel: device?.label ?? null, platform: device?.platform ?? "web", createdAt: s.createdAt, lastUsedAt: s.lastUsedAt };
        });
    },
    async markDeleted(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row && row.deletedAt === null) row.deletedAt = at;
    },
    async takeDown(userId: string, at: Date, deviceId: string | null): Promise<string[]> {
      // One transaction, as the real one: when it fails midway nothing it would have written lands.
      if (faults.has("takeDown")) throw new Error("the take-down transaction failed midway and was rolled back");
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row && row.deletedAt === null) row.deletedAt = at;
      const revoked = takeDownRows(userId, at);
      recordEvent({ userId, type: "account_deleted", deviceId, metadata: {} });
      return revoked;
    },
    async finishTakeDown(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      // As the real statement: only a row marked deleted and not purged yet.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt === null || row.purgedAt !== null) return [];
      return takeDownRows(userId, at);
    },
    // 3f: no address is held in this fake, so a deleted row is always purged.
    async finishPurge(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<"purged" | "held" | "none"> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt === null || row.purgedAt !== null) return "none";
      Object.assign(row, {
        email: `deleted:${userId}`,
        emailVerifiedAt: null,
        passwordHash: null,
        totpSecretEnc: null,
        totpEnabledAt: null,
        recoveryCodesHash: [],
        phoneHash: null,
        ageConfirmedAt: null,
        termsVersion: null,
        termsAcceptedAt: null,
        purgedAt: at,
      });
      return "purged";
    },
    // 3f: what the deletion mail reads of a held address; this fake holds none.
    async addressHold(): Promise<{ until: Date; final: boolean } | null> {
      return null;
    },
  } satisfies Pick<
    AuthRepo,
    | "findUserById"
    | "findUserByEmail"
    | "setPasswordFailures"
    | "createEmailCode"
    | "findEmailCode"
    | "addCodeAttempt"
    | "consumeEmailCode"
    | "changeEmail"
    | "setPasswordHash"
    | "enableTotp"
    | "disableTotp"
    | "lockDown"
    | "setPhoneHash"
    | "appendEvent"
    | "findDeviceById"
    | "ensureWebauthnUserId"
    | "countPasskeys"
    | "listPasskeys"
    | "findPasskey"
    | "recentPasskeyAdditions"
    | "addPasskey"
    | "renamePasskey"
    | "deletePasskey"
    | "findPasskeyByCredentialId"
    | "findPasskeyByCredential"
    | "claimPasskeyUse"
    | "suspectPasskey"
    | "findDevice"
    | "createDevice"
    | "touchDevice"
    | "createSession"
    | "findActiveSession"
    | "rotateSession"
    | "writeFactor"
    | "claimTotpStep"
    | "revokeAllSessions"
    | "listActiveSessions"
    | "markDeleted"
    | "takeDown"
    | "finishTakeDown"
    | "finishPurge"
    | "addressHold"
  >;
  const authRepo = repo as unknown as AuthRepo;
  const kv = new MemoryKv(() => t);
  const mailer = new MemoryMailer();
  /** profiles.verified_at by account, as the badge flows set and clear it through the profile store. */
  const verified = new Map<string, Date | null>();
  /** 3e: the accounts whose suspension runs, as the profile store's predicate would read them; a test adds to it. */
  const suspended = new Set<string>();
  const config: AuthConfig = {
    appOrigin: "http://localhost:8081",
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8081"],
    authHmacKey: Buffer.alloc(32, 3),
    ipHashKey: Buffer.alloc(32, 4),
    totpKey: parseVersionedKey(`v1:${Buffer.alloc(32, 5).toString("base64")}`),
    totpPreviousKeys: [],
    notifierKey: parseVersionedKey(`v1:${Buffer.alloc(32, 6).toString("base64")}`),
    notifierPreviousKeys: [],
    termsVersion: TEST_TERMS,
    trustProxy: "none",
    verifyProvider: "dev",
    webauthn: { rpId: "localhost", rpName: "korbat", origins: ["http://localhost:8081"] },
    // The staff console is off: no flow this harness runs reaches it.
    console: null,
    homeState: null,
    contactPoint: null,
    // 3f Task 5: the report hold, on as by default.
    reportHold: true,
  };
  const deps: AuthDeps = {
    repo: authRepo,
    kv,
    sessions: createSessions({ repo: authRepo, kv, now }),
    lockout: createLockout({ repo: authRepo, kv, now }),
    mailer,
    turnstile: { verify: async () => true },
    breachChecker: { isBreached: async () => false },
    // The flows this harness runs create no profile; the badge flows only set and clear verified_at, kept above by
    // account, and the deletion flow reads the handle, kept by account as `user` registers it. No flow here changes the
    // Explore switch, which reads as the column's default.
    profiles: {
      create: async () => {
        throw new Error("the memory harness has no profile store");
      },
      find: async (id) => {
        const handle = handles.get(id);
        return handle === undefined ? null : { id, handle, displayName: handle, handleChangedAt: null, verified: (verified.get(id) ?? null) !== null, showInExplore: true };
      },
      // 3e: setting the badge is refused while the account's suspension runs, as the predicate refuses the real write.
      setVerified: async (id, at) => {
        if (at !== null && suspended.has(id)) return false;
        verified.set(id, at);
        return true;
      },
      suspended: async (id) => suspended.has(id),
    },
    // The development provider, which accepts exactly 000000; a test swaps it for null or a scripted one.
    verify: devProvider(),
    config,
    log: pino({ level: "silent" }),
    now,
  };
  const ctx: RequestContext = { ipHash: randomToken(), userAgent: undefined };
  /**
   * A live session on a device of its own, both recorded as the deletion flow will find them. It proved an email code
   * just now unless given other factors, as a session behind requireFreshAuth has, and started from no passkey unless told so.
   * The device is a web browser labelled as the sign-in labels one, unless the test says otherwise.
   */
  const session = (userId: string, options: { factors?: Factors; passkeyId?: string | null; platform?: Platform; label?: string | null } = {}): Session => {
    const s: Session = {
      sessionId: sha256Hex(randomToken()),
      userId,
      deviceId: randomUUID(),
      role: "user",
      onboarded: true,
      mfaEnabled: false,
      reauthAt: now(),
      handle: randomUUID(),
      factors: options.factors ?? { email: t },
      passkeyId: options.passkeyId ?? null,
    };
    sessions.push({
      id: s.sessionId,
      userId,
      revokedAt: null,
      deviceId: s.deviceId,
      handle: s.handle,
      factors: s.factors,
      passkeyId: s.passkeyId,
      reauthAt: s.reauthAt,
      createdAt: now(),
      lastUsedAt: now(),
      expiresAt: new Date(t + SESSION_IDLE_MS),
      absoluteExpiresAt: new Date(t + SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MS),
    });
    devices.push({ id: s.deviceId, userId, revokedAt: null, platform: options.platform ?? "web", label: options.label === undefined ? "Chrome on Windows" : options.label });
    return s;
  };
  return {
    deps,
    kv,
    mailer,
    ctx,
    users,
    codes,
    events,
    sessions,
    devices,
    passkeys,
    verified,
    suspended,
    faults,
    now,
    advance(ms: number) {
      t += ms;
    },
    /** Another session of an existing account, on another device. */
    session,
    /**
     * A passkey of an existing account, created at `createdAt` (now unless given) with the row's defaults (a plain,
     * unnamed synced key added from no device) unless overridden; answers its id.
     */
    passkey(userId: string, createdAt: Date = now(), overrides: Partial<Omit<RecordedPasskey, "id" | "userId" | "createdAt">> = {}): string {
      const id = randomUUID();
      passkeys.push({
        id,
        userId,
        createdAt,
        credentialId: randomToken(),
        publicKey: "cose-key",
        counter: 0,
        transports: [],
        backedUp: false,
        name: "Passkey",
        lastUsedAt: null,
        aaguid: null,
        backupEligible: false,
        uvInitialized: false,
        createdDeviceId: null,
        suspectAt: null,
        ...overrides,
      });
      return id;
    },
    /**
     * An onboarded account holding a verified address, with a session that just proved a credential, as a route
     * behind requireFreshAuth passes it on. Its profile's handle is the address's local part unless given.
     */
    user(email: string, handle: string = email.split("@")[0]!.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_]/g, "_")): { user: UserRow; session: Session } {
      const id = randomUUID();
      const user: UserRow = {
        id,
        email,
        emailVerifiedAt: now(),
        phoneHash: null,
        passwordHash: null,
        totpSecretEnc: null,
        totpEnabledAt: null,
        recoveryCodesHash: [],
        failedLogins: 0,
        lockedUntil: null,
        createdAt: now(),
        deletedAt: null,
        role: "user",
        ageConfirmedAt: now(),
        termsVersion: TEST_TERMS,
        termsAcceptedAt: now(),
        onboardedAt: now(),
        passwordChangedAt: null,
        totpLastStep: null,
        purgedAt: null,
        webauthnUserId: null,
      };
      users.set(id, user);
      handles.set(id, handle);
      return { user, session: session(id) };
    },
  };
}

export type MemoryFlowHarness = ReturnType<typeof memoryFlowHarness>;
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { STAFF_USAGE, enrollSettings, migratorUrl, parseStaffArgs, revokeSettings, runStaffCommand, staffDatabaseUrls } from "../src/cli/staff";

const HASH_A = "ab".repeat(32);
const HASH_B = "0123456789abcdef".repeat(4);
const API_URL = "postgres://korbat_api:x@localhost:5432/korbat";
const AUTH_URL = "postgres://korbat_auth:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

/** The command's lines, each marked with the stream it went to. */
function capture() {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  return { lines, out: { log: (line: string) => lines.push(`out ${line}`), error: (line: string) => lines.push(`err ${line}`) } };
}

describe("staff.js arguments", () => {
  test("the usage lists the commands that exist", () => {
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toMatch(/^usage: node dist\/staff\.js <command>/);
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("enroll <email>");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("keys [<email>]");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("audit-head");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("audit-verify [<chain_seq>:<hash> ...]");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("revoke <email> <key id>");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("revoke <email> all");
    // enroll runs as the migrator, in the migrate service; the usage says where.
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toMatch(/run --rm migrate node dist\/staff\.js enroll/);
  });

  test("reads revoke with an email address and a key id or all, normalising both", () => {
    const id = "0f7b3c2e-4a1d-4c6b-9e8f-1a2b3c4d5e6f";
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["revoke", " Mod@Korbat.Local ", "all"])).toEqual({ command: "revoke", email: "mod@korbat.local", key: "all" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", id.toUpperCase()])).toEqual({ command: "revoke", email: "mod@korbat.local", key: id });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", id, "all"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "moderator", "all"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    for (const key of ["ALL", "every", "12", `${id}0`, id.replace(/-/g, "")]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", key]), key).toThrow(`not a key id or all: ${key}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads enroll with one email address and keys with one or none, normalising the address", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["enroll", " Mod@Korbat.Local "])).toEqual({ command: "enroll", email: "mod@korbat.local" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["keys"])).toEqual({ command: "keys", email: null });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["keys", "Mod@Korbat.Local"])).toEqual({ command: "keys", email: "mod@korbat.local" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll", "a@b.io", "b@c.io"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["keys", "a@b.io", "b@c.io"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll", "moderator"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["keys", "all"])).toThrow(`not an email address: all\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
  });

  test("reads audit-head, and audit-verify with any number of kept places", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-head"])).toEqual({ command: "audit-head" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify"])).toEqual({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", `12:${HASH_A}`, `3:${HASH_B}`])).toEqual({
      command: "audit-verify",
      kept: [
        { seq: 12, hash: HASH_A },
        { seq: 3, hash: HASH_B },
      ],
    });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", `999999999999999:${HASH_A}`]).command).toBe("audit-verify");
  });

  test("prints the usage for no command, an unknown one or extra arguments", () => {
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs([])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-tail"])).toThrow(`unknown command: audit-tail\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-head", `1:${HASH_A}`])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
  });

  test("refuses a kept place that is not <chain_seq>:<hash>, a positive place and a lower-case sha256", () => {
    for (const pair of [
      "12",
      `12 ${HASH_A}`,
      `0:${HASH_A}`,
      `-1:${HASH_A}`,
      `01:${HASH_A}`,
      `1.5:${HASH_A}`,
      `1e3:${HASH_A}`,
      `1000000000000000:${HASH_A}`,
      "12:abc",
      `12:${HASH_A.toUpperCase()}`,
      `12:${HASH_A}0`,
      `12:${HASH_A}:1`,
    ]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", pair]), pair).toThrow(`not a kept place: ${pair}`);
    }
  });

  test("run without arguments, it prints its usage and answers 2 before reading any configuration", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand([], {}, out)).toBe(2);
    expect(lines).toEqual([`err ${STAFF_USAGE}`]);
  });
});

// audit-head and audit-verify need no server secret and no console configuration (3a design, section 7), so each reads
// only the database URLs it connects with, never the API's whole configuration.
describe("what each staff.js command reads of the environment", () => {
  test("audit-head reads DATABASE_URL_API alone, and audit-verify that and DATABASE_URL_AUTH", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-head" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL })).toEqual({
      api: API_URL,
      auth: AUTH_URL,
    });
  });

  test("a setting the API's configuration would refuse, the console's included, changes nothing", () => {
    for (const extra of [
      // Not an origin as browsers send it (the final slash).
      { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example/" },
      // The console on the app's own origin.
      { APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081", CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" },
      { CONSOLE_RP_ID: "not a domain" },
      // A secret too short, and production's rules over a development setup.
      { NODE_ENV: "production", AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=", APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" },
    ]) {
      const env = { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...extra };
      expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, env), JSON.stringify(extra)).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: AUTH_URL });
      expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-head" }, env), JSON.stringify(extra)).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    }
  });

  test("names the database URL that is missing or not a PostgreSQL URL, and no other setting", () => {
    const cases: [Parameters<typeof staffDatabaseUrls>[0], Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ command: "audit-head" }, {}, /DATABASE_URL_API/],
      [{ command: "audit-head" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: "mysql://korbat:x@localhost/korbat" }, /DATABASE_URL_API/],
      [{ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "not a url" }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
    ];
    for (const [command, env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        staffDatabaseUrls(command, env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(new RegExp(`^Invalid environment for ${command.command}:`));
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|SMTP_URL|CONSOLE_ORIGIN/);
    }
  });

  test("keys reads DATABASE_URL_AUTH for the keys and DATABASE_URL_API for the handles, and nothing else", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "keys", email: null }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "not an origin" })).toEqual({
      api: API_URL,
      auth: AUTH_URL,
    });
    expect(() => staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "keys", email: "a@b.io" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toThrow(/^Invalid environment for keys:[\s\S]*DATABASE_URL_AUTH/);
  });

  test("run with a database URL missing, it names it and answers 1", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["audit-verify"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for audit-verify:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_AUTH");
    expect(lines[0]).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY/);
  });
});

// enroll runs in the migrate service as the migrator (3a design, section 7): it reads the migrator's database URL and the
// console's origin and relying party ID, which Compose gives that service, and nothing of the API's configuration.
describe("what staff.js enroll reads of the environment", () => {
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

  test("DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE, CONSOLE_ORIGIN and CONSOLE_RP_ID, the relying party ID defaulting to the console's hostname", () => {
    expect(enrollSettings({ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" })).toEqual({
      migrate: MIGRATE_URL,
      consoleOrigin: "http://localhost:8090",
      consoleRpId: "localhost",
    });
    // A blank relying party ID, as Compose passes an empty line of infra/.env, counts as unset.
    expect(enrollSettings({ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example", CONSOLE_RP_ID: " " }).consoleRpId).toBe("console.example");
    expect(enrollSettings({ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "Console.Example" }).consoleRpId).toBe("console.example");
  });

  test("a setting only the API reads, or one the API's configuration would refuse, changes nothing", () => {
    const env = {
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL,
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090",
      // The console on the app's own hostname is refused by the API's rules in production, not here.
      APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081",
      NODE_ENV: "production",
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=",
    };
    expect(enrollSettings(env)).toEqual({ migrate: MIGRATE_URL, consoleOrigin: "http://localhost:8090", consoleRpId: "localhost" });
  });

  test("while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset or blank it refuses, naming it", () => {
    for (const env of [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "" }, { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "  " }]) {
      expect(() => enrollSettings(env), JSON.stringify(env)).toThrow(/CONSOLE_ORIGIN is not set: the staff console is off, so no enrolment link can be issued/);
    }
  });

  test("names the setting that is wrong, and no other", () => {
    const cases: [Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" }, /DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: "mysql://x@localhost/k", CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" }, /DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/],
      // Not an origin as browsers send it: the staff gate would refuse every write the console makes.
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090/" }, /CONSOLE_ORIGIN/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "http://localhost" }, /CONSOLE_RP_ID/],
    ];
    for (const [env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        enrollSettings(env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(/^Invalid environment for enroll:/);
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|SMTP_URL|DATABASE_URL_API|DATABASE_URL_AUTH/);
    }
  });

  test("run while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset, it says so, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    // Nothing listens on port 1: a connection attempt would fail with another message, or hang.
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["enroll", "mod@korbat.local"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@127.0.0.1:1/korbat" }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(2_000);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err .*CONSOLE_ORIGIN is not set/);
  });
});

// revoke runs like grant-role, in the api service (3a design, section 7): it revokes on the auth role and mails the key's
// owner, so it reads the auth role's URL and the mail settings, and nothing else of the API's configuration.
describe("what staff.js revoke reads of the environment", () => {
  const MAIL = { SMTP_URL: "smtp://localhost:1025", MAIL_FROM: "korbat <no-reply@korbat.local>" };

  test("DATABASE_URL_AUTH, SMTP_URL and MAIL_FROM, with TLS required from a plain relay in production as the API requires it", () => {
    expect(revokeSettings({ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...MAIL })).toEqual({ auth: AUTH_URL, mail: { smtpUrl: MAIL.SMTP_URL, mailFrom: MAIL.MAIL_FROM, requireTls: false } });
    expect(revokeSettings({ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...MAIL, NODE_ENV: "production" }).mail.requireTls).toBe(true);
  });

  test("a setting only the API reads, or one the API's configuration would refuse, changes nothing", () => {
    const env = { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...MAIL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example/", APP_ORIGIN: "not a url", AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=", DATABASE_URL_API: "nope" };
    expect(revokeSettings(env).auth).toBe(AUTH_URL);
  });

  test("names the setting that is missing or wrong, and no other", () => {
    const cases: [Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ ...MAIL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "mysql://x@localhost/k", ...MAIL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, MAIL_FROM: MAIL.MAIL_FROM }, /SMTP_URL/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, SMTP_URL: "http://localhost:1025", MAIL_FROM: MAIL.MAIL_FROM }, /SMTP_URL/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, SMTP_URL: MAIL.SMTP_URL }, /MAIL_FROM/],
    ];
    for (const [env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        revokeSettings(env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(/^Invalid environment for revoke:/);
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|CONSOLE_ORIGIN|DATABASE_URL_API|DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/);
    }
  });

  test("run with a setting missing, it names it, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", "all"], { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "postgres://korbat_auth:x@127.0.0.1:1/korbat", ...MAIL, SMTP_URL: "" }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(2_000);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for revoke:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("SMTP_URL");
  });
});

describe("staff.js: the commands for moderation cases (3c design, section 7.13)", () => {
  const CASE = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

  test("the usage lists them, and says which run in the migrate service", () => {
    for (const words of ["text-verify", "access-request <@handle | email>", "link <staff email> <personal handle>", "unlink <staff email> <personal handle>", "limits <decisions per hour> <decisions per day> <case opens per day> <findings per day> <reveals per day>"]) {
      expect(STAFF_USAGE, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("linked to it");
    // 3f Task 5: notification-facts replaces account-facts, and the record commands are listed with the order commands.
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).not.toContain("account-facts");
    for (const words of ["records [--verify]", "notification-facts <record>", "notification-sent <record>", "production-account <order>", "address-check --handle <handle> < address", "handover-list <seal action>", "handover-record <production>", "handover-destroyed <production>"]) {
      expect(STAFF_USAGE, words).toContain(`  ${words}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads link and unlink with a staff address and a personal handle, with or without its at sign, in lower case", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["link", " Mod@Korbat.Local ", "@Ada_L"])).toEqual({ command: "link", email: "mod@korbat.local", handle: "ada_l" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", "ada_l"])).toEqual({ command: "unlink", email: "mod@korbat.local", handle: "ada_l" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["link", "mod@korbat.local"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["link", "mod@korbat.local", "ada", "bob"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["link", "moderator", "ada"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    for (const handle of ["ada lovelace", "ada@korbat.local", "@", "a-b", "'; drop table profiles; --"]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", handle]), handle).toThrow(`not a handle: ${handle}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads limits with exactly five whole numbers from 1, in the order of the usage", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10"])).toEqual({
      command: "limits",
      limits: { decisionsPerHour: 60, decisionsPerDay: 300, caseOpensPerDay: 400, findingsPerDay: 50, revealsPerDay: 10 },
    });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10", "5"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    for (const number of ["0", "-1", "1.5", "1e3", "ten", "", " 5", "05", "12345678"]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", number, "50", "10"]), JSON.stringify(number)).toThrow(`not a limit: ${number}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads text-verify without arguments, the record commands with what they name and their flags, and access-request with a handle or an address", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["text-verify"])).toEqual({ command: "text-verify" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["text-verify", "now"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    // 3f Task 5: account-facts is gone; notification-facts names a record.
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["account-facts", "@Ada", CASE])).toThrow("unknown command: account-facts");
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["notification-facts", CASE])).toEqual({ command: "record", record: { command: "notification-facts", target: CASE, positional: [], flags: new Map() } });
    const sent = parseStaffArgs(["notification-sent", CASE, "--duty", "dsa18_1", "--duty", "tco14_5", "--kinds", "handle,address"]);
    expect(sent).toMatchObject({ command: "record", record: { command: "notification-sent", target: CASE } });
    expect((sent as { record: { flags: Map<string, string[]> } }).record.flags.get("--duty")).toEqual(["dsa18_1", "tco14_5"]);
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["records", "--verify"])).toMatchObject({ command: "record", record: { command: "records", target: null } });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["records", CASE])).toThrow(/records: takes no/);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["notification-facts"])).toThrow(/notification-facts: name the record/);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["handover-list", "--instrument"])).toThrow(/needs a value/);
    // An at sign in front is a handle's; one inside is an address's.
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "@Ada"])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { handle: "ada" } });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada"])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { handle: "ada" } });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", " Ada@Korbat.Local "])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { email: "ada@korbat.local" } });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada", "bob"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada lovelace"])).toThrow("not a handle: ada lovelace");
  });

  test("text-verify reads DATABASE_URL_API alone; link, unlink and limits the migrator's URL alone", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "text-verify" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    expect(() => staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "text-verify" }, { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL })).toThrow(/DATABASE_URL_API/);
    expect(migratorUrl("limits", { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "not an origin", SMTP_URL: "nonsense" })).toBe(MIGRATE_URL);
    expect(() => migratorUrl("link", { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toThrow(/Invalid environment for link:[^]*DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/);
  });

  test("run in the wrong service, each says which URL it lacks, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    for (const args of [["link", "mod@korbat.local", "ada"], ["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", "ada"], ["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10"], ["records"], ["notification-facts", CASE]]) {
      const { lines, out } = capture();
      expect(await runStaffCommand(args, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, out), args[0]).toBe(1);
      expect(lines, args[0]).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(lines[0], args[0]).toMatch(new RegExp(`^err Invalid environment for ${args[0]}:`));
      expect(lines[0], args[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE");
    }
    // access-request for an address reads the API's whole configuration, and refuses with what is missing of it.
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "ada@korbat.local"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err /);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_API");
    // 3f Task 5: for a handle it runs in the migrate service, which holds the migrator's URL and APP_ORIGIN.
    const handle = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "@ada"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, handle.out)).toBe(1);
    expect(handle.lines).toEqual(["err access-request: a handle's draft runs in the migrate service, which holds DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE and APP_ORIGIN; nothing was drafted"]);
    const noOrigin = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "@ada"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, noOrigin.out)).toBe(1);
    expect(noOrigin.lines).toEqual(handle.lines);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { authConfigFrom } from "../src/auth/context";
import { loadConfig } from "../src/config";

const key = Buffer.alloc(32, 7).toString("base64");

const good = {
  DATABASE_URL_API: "postgres://korbat_api:x@localhost:5432/korbat",
  DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "postgres://korbat_auth:x@localhost:5432/korbat",
  REDIS_URL: "redis://localhost:6379",
  APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081",
  AUTH_HMAC_KEY: key,
  IP_HASH_KEY: key,
  TOTP_ENC_KEY: `v1:${key}`,
  NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: `v1:${key}`,
  TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: "1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA",
  SMTP_URL: "smtp://localhost:1025",
  MAIL_FROM: "korbat <no-reply@korbat.local>",
  TERMS_VERSION: "draft-2026-09",
};

describe("loadConfig", () => {
  test("applies defaults", () => {
    const c = loadConfig(good);
    expect(c.PORT).toBe(3000);
    expect(c.NODE_ENV).toBe("development");
    expect(c.TRUSTED_ORIGINS).toEqual([]);
  });
  test("parses trusted origins list", () => {
    expect(loadConfig({ ...good, TRUSTED_ORIGINS: "http://a.test, http://b.test" }).TRUSTED_ORIGINS).toEqual(["http://a.test", "http://b.test"]);
  });
  test("fails loudly on a missing database url", () => {
    expect(() => loadConfig({ REDIS_URL: good.REDIS_URL })).toThrow(/DATABASE_URL_API/);
  });
  test("rejects keys shorter than 32 bytes", () => {
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, AUTH_HMAC_KEY: Buffer.alloc(16).toString("base64") })).toThrow(/AUTH_HMAC_KEY/);
  });
  test("TOTP key must be versioned and exactly 32 bytes", () => {
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, TOTP_ENC_KEY: key })).toThrow(/TOTP_ENC_KEY/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, TOTP_ENC_KEY: `v1:${Buffer.alloc(33).toString("base64")}` })).toThrow(/TOTP_ENC_KEY/);
  });
  test("the notifier key must be versioned and exactly 32 bytes, as the TOTP key is", () => {
    expect(loadConfig(good).NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY).toBe(`v1:${key}`);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: key })).toThrow(/NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: `v1:${Buffer.alloc(33).toString("base64")}` })).toThrow(/NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY/);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: "" })).toThrow(/NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY/);
  });
  test("previous notifier keys are optional, comma-separated and each versioned", () => {
    expect(loadConfig(good).NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS).toEqual([]);
    expect(loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: "" }).NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS).toEqual([]);
    expect(loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: `v0:${key}, v1:${key}` }).NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS).toEqual([`v0:${key}`, `v1:${key}`]);
    expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: key })).toThrow(/NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS/);
  });
  test("the auth configuration holds the notifier key and the keys it replaced, parsed", () => {
    const older = Buffer.alloc(32, 9).toString("base64");
    const auth = authConfigFrom(loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: `v2:${key}`, NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: `v1:${older}` }));
    expect(auth.notifierKey).toEqual({ version: "v2", key: Buffer.alloc(32, 7) });
    expect(auth.notifierPreviousKeys).toEqual([{ version: "v1", key: Buffer.alloc(32, 9) }]);
    expect(authConfigFrom(loadConfig(good)).notifierPreviousKeys).toEqual([]);
  });
  describe("the moderation settings", () => {
    test("MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR is an hour of the UTC day, 7 unless set; a blank value is the default", () => {
      expect(loadConfig(good).MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR).toBe(7);
      for (const blank of ["", "   "]) expect(loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: blank }).MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR, JSON.stringify(blank)).toBe(7);
      for (const [written, hour] of [["0", 0], ["7", 7], ["23", 23], [" 12 ", 12]] as const) {
        expect(loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: written }).MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR, written).toBe(hour);
      }
      for (const refused of ["24", "-1", "7.5", "yes"]) {
        expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: refused }), refused).toThrow(/MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR/);
      }
    });
    test("MODERATION_RETENTION is on unless set to off; a blank value is on and nothing else is taken", () => {
      expect(loadConfig(good).MODERATION_RETENTION).toBe("on");
      // Compose passes an empty line of infra/.env as an empty value: a blank must never read as "off", which stops every erasure.
      for (const blank of ["", " ", "   "]) expect(loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_RETENTION: blank }).MODERATION_RETENTION, JSON.stringify(blank)).toBe("on");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_RETENTION: "on" }).MODERATION_RETENTION).toBe("on");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_RETENTION: "off" }).MODERATION_RETENTION).toBe("off");
      for (const refused of ["yes", "no", "true", "false", "1", "0", "ON", "Off", "paused"]) {
        expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_RETENTION: refused }), refused).toThrow(/MODERATION_RETENTION/);
      }
    });

    test("3f: HOME_STATE is a state korbat has facts for, CONTACT_POINT an address; both unset by default, and the home state required once the contact point is set", () => {
      expect(loadConfig(good).HOME_STATE).toBeUndefined();
      expect(loadConfig(good).CONTACT_POINT).toBeUndefined();
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, HOME_STATE: " " }).HOME_STATE).toBeUndefined();
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, HOME_STATE: "DE" }).HOME_STATE).toBe("DE");
      // A member state whose facts are not filled in, a code that is no member state, and a lower-case one are refused.
      for (const refused of ["AT", "US", "de"]) expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, HOME_STATE: refused }), refused).toThrow(/HOME_STATE/);
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, HOME_STATE: "DE", CONTACT_POINT: "orders@korbat.example" }).CONTACT_POINT).toBe("orders@korbat.example");
      expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, CONTACT_POINT: "orders@korbat.example" })).toThrow(/HOME_STATE/);
      expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, HOME_STATE: "DE", CONTACT_POINT: "not an address" })).toThrow(/CONTACT_POINT/);
    });

    test("3f: NOTIFY is off by default outside production and on in production; a blank value is the default, and nothing but on and off is taken", () => {
      expect(loadConfig(good).NOTIFY).toBe("off");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFY: " " }).NOTIFY).toBe("off");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFY: "on" }).NOTIFY).toBe("on");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, NODE_ENV: "test" }).NOTIFY).toBe("off");
      for (const refused of ["yes", "1", "ON", "Off"]) expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, NOTIFY: refused }), refused).toThrow(/NOTIFY/);
    });
    test("3f Task 5: REPORT_HOLD is on unless set to off; a blank value is the default, and nothing but on and off is taken", () => {
      expect(loadConfig(good).REPORT_HOLD).toBe("on");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, REPORT_HOLD: " " }).REPORT_HOLD).toBe("on");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, REPORT_HOLD: "off" }).REPORT_HOLD).toBe("off");
      for (const refused of ["no", "0", "OFF"]) expect(() => loadConfig({ ...good, REPORT_HOLD: refused }), refused).toThrow(/REPORT_HOLD/);
    });

    test("MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN is off unless set to on; a blank value is the default and nothing else is taken", () => {
      expect(loadConfig(good).MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN).toBe("off");
      expect(loadConfig({ ...good, MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: "" }).MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN).toBe("off");
```

```ts
/**
 * Account deletion across the three modules on real Postgres: the auth repository behind the auth
 * flows, the social repository's purge, the media repository with both volumes in a temporary
 * directory, composed the way the server composes the account module's dependencies from the module
 * indexes. The auth flows read the handle through the real profile store, as the server wires it.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: account deletion", () => {
  let apiDb: Db;
  let authDb: Db;
  /** 3e: profiles.created_at is no longer the API role's to write (migration 0020 grants it the columns it writes), so the migrator ages the profile. */
  let migrateDb: Db;
  let authRepo: AuthRepo;
  let h: FlowHarness;
  let m: MediaHarness;
  let s: SocialHarness;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const config = loadConfig();
    apiDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 4 });
    authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH, { max: 4 });
    migrateDb = createDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE!, { max: 1 });
    authRepo = createAuthRepo(authDb);
    h = flowHarness(authRepo, { profiles: createProfileStore(apiDb) });
    m = await mediaHarness(apiDb);
    s = socialHarness(apiDb, {
      media: {
        attach: (tx, input) => m.deps.repo.attach(tx, input),
        detachAll: (tx, postId) => m.deps.repo.detachAll(tx, postId),
        requestDeletion: (ids) => m.files.requestDeletion(ids),
        forPosts: (postIds) => m.deps.repo.forPosts(postIds),
      },
    });
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    m.cleanup();
    await Promise.all([closeDb(apiDb), closeDb(authDb), closeDb(migrateDb)]);
  });

  const deps = (): AccountDeps => ({
    auth: {
      startDeletion: (session, ctx) => authStartDeletion(h.deps, session, ctx),
      confirmDeletion: (session, input) => authConfirmDeletion(h.deps, session, input),
      pendingPurges: () => authRepo.pendingPurges(),
      finishPurge: (userId) => authRepo.finishPurge(userId, new Date()),
      takeDownTerminated: (userId, facts) => takeDownTerminated(h.deps, userId, facts),
      exportAccount: (userId) => exportAccount(h.deps, userId),
      appendEvent: (userId, type, metadata) => authRepo.appendEvent({ userId, type, metadata }),
    },
    social: {
      purgeProfile: (userId, now, within) => s.repo.purgeProfile(userId, now, within),
      exportProfile: (userId) => exportProfile(s.deps, userId),
    },
    // The media module's own interface for this one, over the harness's repository and volumes.
    media: mediaForAccount(m.deps),
    limits: new MemoryStore(),
    log: pino({ level: "silent" }),
    now: () => new Date(),
  });

  /** An auth account with a password, signed in on one device, with a profile of the same id in the public schema, old enough to quote and repost. */
  async function account() {
    const owner = await onboardedUser(h, authRepo, { password: PASSWORD });
    const handle = newHandle();
    const created = await createProfileStore(apiDb).create({ id: owner.user.id, handle, displayName: "Owner" });
    expect(created.ok).toBe(true);
    await migrateDb.update(profiles).set({ createdAt: new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 24 * 60 * 60_000) }).where(eq(profiles.id, owner.user.id));
    return { ...owner, handle };
  }

  const authRow = async (id: string) => (await authDb.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, id)))[0];
  const profileRow = async (id: string) => (await apiDb.select().from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.id, id)))[0]!;
  const postRow = async (id: string) => (await apiDb.select().from(posts).where(eq(posts.id, id)))[0]!;
  const rowCount = async (table: typeof likes | typeof reposts | typeof bookmarks, userId: string) =>
    (await apiDb.select({ n: count() }).from(table).where(eq(table.userId, userId)))[0]!.n;
  const pairCount = async (table: typeof follows | typeof blocks | typeof mutes, id: string) =>
    (await apiDb.select({ n: count() }).from(table).where(sql`${table.fromId} = ${id}::uuid or ${table.toId} = ${id}::uuid`))[0]!.n;
  const image = (id: string, alt: string) => ({ id, alt });

  test("deleting an account with posts, images, engagement and graph rows leaves tombstones, right counters elsewhere, no image rows, an anonymised profile with its handle reserved, and an anonymised auth row", async () => {
    const owner = await account();
    const userId = owner.user.id;
    // The handle left behind stays reserved, and so does the current one.
    const renamed = newHandle();
    expect((await s.repo.changeHandle(userId, renamed, s.clock.next())).ok).toBe(true);
    const other = await signIn(h.deps, owner.user, owner.device, h.ctx, { alertNewDevice: false, factors: { email: h.clock.ms() }, method: "email" });
    await authRepo.createEmailCode({ flowId: randomBytes(16).toString("hex"), email: owner.email, userId, purpose: "reauth", codeHash: "h", expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 600_000), ipHash: "x" });
    await authRepo.setPhoneHash(userId, randomBytes(16).toString("hex"));
    await h.deps.profiles.setVerified(userId, new Date());

    const [bob, carol, dan, eve] = await Promise.all([s.established(), s.established(), s.established(), s.established()]);
    const bobsPost = await createPost(s.deps, bob.id, { body: "bob's post", media: [] });
    const [imageA, imageB] = [await m.readyImage(userId), await m.readyImage(userId)];
    const root = await createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "two photos", media: [image(imageA, "a harbour at dawn"), image(imageB, "a lighthouse")] });
    const selfReply = await createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "my own follow-up", replyToId: root.id, media: [] });
    const replyToBob = await createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "a reply to bob", replyToId: bobsPost.id, media: [] });
    const quoteOfBob = await createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "quoting bob", quoteOfId: bobsPost.id, media: [] });
    const earlier = await createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "deleted before the account", media: [] });
    await deletePost(s.deps, userId, earlier.id);
    const earlierDeletedAt = (await postRow(earlier.id)).deletedAt;
    const bobsReply = await createPost(s.deps, bob.id, { body: "bob replies", replyToId: root.id, media: [] });
    // Engagement: the owner's on bob's post goes with the counters; carol's stays, so the counters come down to one, not to zero.
    for (const who of [userId, carol.id]) expect(await s.repo.like(who, bobsPost.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.repost(userId, bobsPost.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.bookmark(userId, bobsPost.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.like(carol.id, root.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    // The graph: follows both ways with a bystander on each side, a block each way, a mute each way.
    for (const [from, to] of [
      [userId, bob.id],
      [bob.id, userId],
      [carol.id, userId],
      [carol.id, bob.id],
      [bob.id, carol.id],
    ]) {
      expect(await s.repo.follow(from!, to!, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    }
    expect(await s.repo.block(userId, dan.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.block(eve.id, userId, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.mute(userId, carol.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.mute(dan.id, userId, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    // Uploads on no post, in every state: they go too, files and all.
    const loose = await m.readyImage(userId);
    const processing = (await upload(m.deps, userId, m.jpeg())).id;
    const failed = (await upload(m.deps, userId, m.jpeg())).id;
    m.worker.failed(failed, "corrupt_image");
    await status(m.deps, userId, failed);
    // The upload still in processing has its file waiting in the uploads volume for the worker.
    expect(existsSync(m.files.uploads.upload(processing))).toBe(true);

    expect(await profileRow(bob.id)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 2, followingCount: 2, postCount: 1 });
    expect(await profileRow(carol.id)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 1, followingCount: 2 });
    expect(await postRow(bobsPost.id)).toMatchObject({ likeCount: 2, repostCount: 1, replyCount: 1, quoteCount: 1 });
    expect(await profileRow(userId)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 2, followingCount: 1, postCount: 2 });

    const { flowId } = await startDeletion(deps(), owner.session, h.ctx);
    const code = h.mailer.lastCodeFor(owner.email)!;
    await confirmDeletion(deps(), owner.session, { flowId, code, handle: renamed.toUpperCase() });

    // The auth row: gone for every lookup, anonymised, both sessions dead and tombstoned, no devices or codes, the event recorded, the notice sent.
    expect(await authRepo.findUserById(userId)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(await authRepo.findUserByEmail(owner.email)).toBeUndefined();
    const anonymised = (await authRow(userId))!;
    expect(anonymised.deletedAt).not.toBeNull();
    expect(anonymised.purgedAt).not.toBeNull();
    expect(anonymised).toMatchObject({
      email: `deleted:${userId}`,
      emailVerifiedAt: null,
      passwordHash: null,
      totpSecretEnc: null,
      totpEnabledAt: null,
      recoveryCodesHash: [],
      phoneHash: null,
      ageConfirmedAt: null,
      termsVersion: null,
      termsAcceptedAt: null,
    });
    for (const id of [owner.session.sessionId, other.issued.session.sessionId]) {
      expect(await authRepo.findActiveSession(id, new Date()), id).toBeUndefined();
      expect(await h.kv.get(`sess:2:${id}`), id).toBe("revoked");
    }
    expect(await authRepo.listDevices(userId)).toEqual([]);
    expect((await authDb.execute(sql`select count(*)::int as n from auth.email_codes where user_id = ${userId}::uuid`)) as unknown as { n: number }[]).toEqual([{ n: 0 }]);
    expect((await authRepo.recentEvents(userId)).map((e) => e.type)).toContain("account_deleted");
    expect(h.mailer.sent.filter((mail) => mail.to === owner.email).map((mail) => mail.template)).toEqual(["delete_account_code", "account_deleted"]);

    // The profile: not found by either handle, anonymised, its handles still reserved for it.
    expect(await s.repo.findProfileByHandle(renamed)).toBeNull();
    expect(await s.repo.findProfileByHandle(owner.handle)).toBeNull();
    expect(await rejection(profile(s.deps, null, renamed))).toBe("not_found");
    expect(await rejection(exportProfile(s.deps, userId))).toBe("not_found");
    const gone = await profileRow(userId);
    expect(gone).toMatchObject({ handle: renamed, displayName: "Deleted account", bio: "", avatarPath: null, verifiedAt: null, followerCount: 0, followingCount: 0, postCount: 0 });
    expect(gone.deletedAt).not.toBeNull();
    expect((await apiDb.select({ handle: handleHistory.handleLower }).from(handleHistory).where(eq(handleHistory.profileId, userId))).map((row) => row.handle).sort()).toEqual([owner.handle, renamed].sort());
    expect(await s.repo.changeHandle(bob.id, renamed, s.clock.next())).toEqual({ ok: false, reason: "handle_taken" });
    expect(await s.repo.changeHandle(bob.id, owner.handle, s.clock.next())).toEqual({ ok: false, reason: "handle_taken" });

    // Every post is a tombstone; the one deleted earlier keeps its time; parents and quoted posts count them no more.
    for (const id of [root.id, selfReply.id, replyToBob.id, quoteOfBob.id, earlier.id]) {
      expect(await postRow(id), id).toMatchObject({ state: "deleted_by_author", body: "" });
      expect((await postRow(id)).deletedAt, id).not.toBeNull();
      expect(await rejection(getPost(s.deps, null, id)), id).toBe("not_found");
    }
    expect((await postRow(earlier.id)).deletedAt).toEqual(earlierDeletedAt);
    expect(await postRow(bobsPost.id)).toMatchObject({ likeCount: 1, repostCount: 0, replyCount: 0, quoteCount: 0 });
    expect((await thread(s.deps, null, bobsReply.id, page)).ancestors).toEqual([{ id: root.id, deleted: true }]);
    expect((await latestTimeline(s.deps, null, page)).items.map((item) => item.post.id)).not.toContain(root.id);
    expect(await postRow(bobsReply.id)).toMatchObject({ state: "visible", replyToId: root.id });

    // The owner's engagement and graph rows are gone, in both directions, and the other accounts' counters follow.
    for (const table of [likes, reposts, bookmarks]) expect(await rowCount(table, userId)).toBe(0);
    for (const table of [follows, blocks, mutes]) expect(await pairCount(table, userId)).toBe(0);
    expect(await rowCount(likes, carol.id)).toBe(2);
    expect(await profileRow(bob.id)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 1, followingCount: 1, postCount: 1 });
    expect(await profileRow(carol.id)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 1, followingCount: 1 });
    expect((await s.repo.relation(eve.id, userId)).blocked).toBe(false);
    expect((await s.repo.relation(dan.id, userId)).muted).toBe(false);

    // The image rows are gone whatever their state, and the worker is asked for every file.
    for (const id of [imageA, imageB, loose, processing, failed]) expect(await m.deps.repo.find(id), id).toBeNull();
    expect(await m.deps.repo.readyImages(userId)).toEqual([]);
    expect(await m.files.deletionRequests()).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([imageA, imageB, loose, processing, failed]));
    // On the disk: every id has its request, and the processing upload's file is gone, so no worker picks it up afterwards.
    for (const id of [imageA, imageB, loose, processing, failed]) expect(existsSync(m.files.uploads.deletion(id)), id).toBe(true);
    for (const id of [imageA, imageB, loose, processing, failed]) expect(existsSync(m.files.uploads.upload(id)), id).toBe(false);
    expect(await authRepo.pendingPurges()).not.toContain(userId);

    // A second purge changes nothing: the rows read the same afterwards, and no further file deletion is asked for.
    const before = { auth: await authRow(userId), profile: gone, bob: await profileRow(bob.id), bobsPost: await postRow(bobsPost.id), requests: (await m.files.deletionRequests()).sort() };
    await purge(deps(), userId);
    expect({ auth: await authRow(userId), profile: await profileRow(userId), bob: await profileRow(bob.id), bobsPost: await postRow(bobsPost.id), requests: (await m.files.deletionRequests()).sort() }).toEqual(before);
  });

  test("3e: a suspended account deletes itself its 1b way, with no hold: the purge takes the rows of its followers and those it follows before any post, writes their counters exactly, and writes no standing into the deleted row", async () => {
    const owner = await account();
    const userId = owner.user.id;
    const [bob, carol] = await Promise.all([s.established(), s.established()]);
    const own = await createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "posted before the suspension", media: [] });
    expect(await s.repo.follow(bob.id, userId, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.follow(userId, carol.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    await suspendRowForTest(migrateDb, userId);
    // The suspended account cannot post, but it can delete itself (GDPR Art. 17): no hold (3e design, section 2, row 27).
    expect(await rejection(createPost(s.deps, userId, { body: "while suspended", media: [] }))).toBe("account_suspended");
    const { flowId } = await startDeletion(deps(), owner.session, h.ctx);
    await confirmDeletion(deps(), owner.session, { flowId, code: h.mailer.lastCodeFor(owner.email)!, handle: owner.handle });
    expect((await authRow(userId))!.purgedAt).not.toBeNull();
    expect(await profileRow(userId)).toMatchObject({ displayName: "Deleted account", followerCount: 0, followingCount: 0, postCount: 0 });
    expect(await postRow(own.id)).toMatchObject({ state: "deleted_by_author", body: "" });
    expect(await profileRow(bob.id)).toMatchObject({ followingCount: 0 });
    expect(await profileRow(carol.id)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 0 });
  });

  test("3e: the take-down of a terminated account, as the system: the row marked deleted and its sessions revoked as a confirmation leaves them, the event marked a termination's, termination_final to the address read before it and never account_deleted; a second call changes and mails nothing, and the round's purge finishes it", async () => {
    const owner = await account();
    const userId = owner.user.id;
    const decidedAt = new Date("2026-04-04T09:30:15.250Z");
    expect(await takeDownTerminated(h.deps, userId, { decidedAt, imagesSealed: true })).toBe(true);
    expect((await authRow(userId))!.deletedAt).not.toBeNull();
    expect(await authRepo.findActiveSession(owner.session.sessionId, new Date())).toBeUndefined();
    const mailed = () => h.mailer.sent.filter((mail) => mail.to === owner.email);
    expect(mailed().map((mail) => mail.template)).toEqual(["termination_final"]);
    expect(mailed()[0]!.data).toEqual({ decided: "2026-04-04 09:30 UTC", imagesSealed: "true" });
    const [event] = await migrateDb.execute<{ metadata: Record<string, unknown> }>(sql`select metadata from auth.auth_events where user_id = ${userId}::uuid and type = 'account_deleted'`);
    expect(event?.metadata).toEqual({ terminated: true });
    // Once only: the account is already marked deleted, so nothing is written and nothing mailed.
    expect(await takeDownTerminated(h.deps, userId, { decidedAt, imagesSealed: true })).toBe(false);
    expect(mailed()).toHaveLength(1);
    // The round's purge finds it among the deletions left to finish, as any other.
    expect(await authRepo.pendingPurges()).toContain(userId);
    const report = await purgePending(deps());
    expect(report).toMatchObject({ failed: 0, terminated: 0 });
    expect((await authRow(userId))!.purgedAt).not.toBeNull();
  });

  test("sign-in with a deleted address behaves as for an unknown one before the purge ran, and one round of the job finishes deletions left half done, oldest first", async () => {
    const ghost = await account();
    const later = await account();
    const bob = await s.established();
    const ghostsPost = await createPost(s.deps, ghost.user.id, { body: "left behind", media: [] });
    expect(await s.repo.follow(bob.id, ghost.user.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    expect(await s.repo.follow(ghost.user.id, bob.id, s.clock.next())).toBe(true);
    // Deleted by hand, as a process that died after the auth step leaves them: no purge has run.
    await authRepo.markDeleted(ghost.user.id, new Date(Date.now() - 120_000));
    await authRepo.markDeleted(later.user.id, new Date(Date.now() - 60_000));

    // The start answers as for an address without an account, and the right password no longer signs in.
    const device = newTestDevice();
    const started = await startEmail(h.deps, { email: ghost.email, turnstileToken: "ok", ...device }, h.ctx);
    expect(Object.keys(started)).toEqual(["flowId"]);
    expect((await authRepo.findEmailCode(started.flowId))?.purpose).toBe("signup");
    expect(h.mailer.sent.filter((mail) => mail.to === ghost.email).map((mail) => mail.template)).toEqual(["sign_up_code"]);
    expect(await rejection(passwordSignIn(h.deps, { email: ghost.email, password: PASSWORD, turnstileToken: "ok", ...device }, h.ctx))).toBe("invalid_credentials");
    expect(await authRepo.findActiveSession(ghost.session.sessionId, new Date())).toBeUndefined();
    // The profile is still there for the moment; the job is what takes it down.
    expect(await s.repo.findProfileByHandle(ghost.handle)).not.toBeNull();

    const pending = await authRepo.pendingPurges();
    expect(pending).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([ghost.user.id, later.user.id]));
    expect(pending.indexOf(ghost.user.id)).toBeLessThan(pending.indexOf(later.user.id));
    const report = await purgePending(deps());
    expect(report.failed).toBe(0);
    expect(report.purged).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(await authRepo.pendingPurges()).toEqual([]);
    for (const user of [ghost, later]) {
      const row = (await authRow(user.user.id))!;
      expect(row.purgedAt, user.handle).not.toBeNull();
      expect(row.email, user.handle).toBe(`deleted:${user.user.id}`);
      expect(await s.repo.findProfileByHandle(user.handle), user.handle).toBeNull();
      expect(await profileRow(user.user.id)).toMatchObject({ displayName: "Deleted account", followerCount: 0, followingCount: 0, postCount: 0 });
    }
    expect(await postRow(ghostsPost.id)).toMatchObject({ state: "deleted_by_author", body: "" });
    expect(await profileRow(bob.id)).toMatchObject({ followerCount: 0, followingCount: 0 });
    // The job as the server runs it: a round under its lock, with nothing left to do.
    expect(await createPurgeJob(deps(), new MemoryJobLock()).round()).toBe("ran");

    // finishPurge twice is once: the second call leaves the row as it was; and it never touches a live account.
    const purged = await authRow(ghost.user.id);
    await authRepo.finishPurge(ghost.user.id, new Date(Date.now() + 1000));
    expect(await authRow(ghost.user.id)).toEqual(purged);
    const alive = await account();
    await authRepo.finishPurge(alive.user.id, new Date());
    expect(await authRow(alive.user.id)).toMatchObject({ email: alive.email, purgedAt: null, deletedAt: null });
    expect(await authRepo.findUserById(alive.user.id)).toBeDefined();
  });

  test("3f: with an address held for a report, the deletion takes everything down at once but the address: the credentials go in the purge's first statement, the address and purged_at wait, the mail gains the hold's paragraph, and the next round after the hold is released overwrites the address", async () => {
    const owner = await account();
    const userId = owner.user.id;
    await authRepo.setPhoneHash(userId, randomBytes(16).toString("hex"));
    // A seal taken while deciding holds the account's record: its hold, as report_open sets it, written as the migrator.
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into auth.report_holds (user_id, set_at, seal_final) values (${userId}::uuid, now(), false)`);
    try {
      const { flowId } = await startDeletion(deps(), owner.session, h.ctx);
      await confirmDeletion(deps(), owner.session, { flowId, code: h.mailer.lastCodeFor(owner.email)!, handle: owner.handle });
      // Everything but the address went at once: the credentials and personal facts, the profile, the sessions.
      const held = (await authRow(userId))!;
      expect(held).toMatchObject({ email: owner.email, purgedAt: null, passwordHash: null, totpSecretEnc: null, phoneHash: null, recoveryCodesHash: [], ageConfirmedAt: null, termsVersion: null, termsAcceptedAt: null });
      expect(held.deletedAt).not.toBeNull();
      expect(await s.repo.findProfileByHandle(owner.handle)).toBeNull();
      // The mail: the one wording for every account, and the paragraph of the seal taken while deciding, with its day.
      const mail = h.mailer.sent.filter((m) => m.to === owner.email && m.template === "account_deleted").at(-1)!;
      const [until] = await migrateDb.execute<{ day: string }>(sql`select to_char(auth.address_held_until(${userId}::uuid) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as day`);
      expect(mail.data).toEqual({ heldUntil: until!.day, holdFinal: "false" });
      // The account stays pending, last, and each round counts it as held and changes nothing.
      const first = await purgePending(deps());
      expect(first.held).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
      expect(await authRow(userId)).toMatchObject({ email: owner.email, purgedAt: null });
      const pending = await authRepo.pendingPurges();
      expect(pending.at(-1)).toBe(userId);
      // The record is sent: the hold is released, and the next round overwrites the address.
      await migrateDb.execute(sql`update auth.report_holds set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'sent' where user_id = ${userId}::uuid`);
      await purgePending(deps());
      expect(await authRow(userId)).toMatchObject({ email: `deleted:${userId}`, emailVerifiedAt: null });
      expect((await authRow(userId))!.purgedAt).not.toBeNull();
    } finally {
      await migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from auth.report_holds where user_id = ${userId}::uuid`);
    }
  });

  test("3f: a hold older than reportHoldDays reads as not held, and REPORT_HOLD off purges a held address at once, as 1b did", async () => {
    const aged = await account();
    const off = await account();
    for (const user of [aged, off]) {
      await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into auth.report_holds (user_id, set_at, seal_final) values (${user.user.id}::uuid, now(), true)`);
      await authRepo.markDeleted(user.user.id, new Date(Date.now() - 60_000));
    }
    try {
      expect(await authRepo.finishPurge(aged.user.id, new Date())).toBe("held");
      await migrateDb.execute(sql`update auth.report_holds set set_at = set_at - make_interval(days => ${ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays}, secs => 1) where user_id = ${aged.user.id}::uuid`);
      expect(await authRepo.finishPurge(aged.user.id, new Date())).toBe("purged");
      expect(await authRepo.finishPurge(off.user.id, new Date(), false)).toBe("purged");
      expect(await authRow(off.user.id)).toMatchObject({ email: `deleted:${off.user.id}` });
      expect(await authRepo.finishPurge(off.user.id, new Date())).toBe("none");
    } finally {
      await migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from auth.report_holds where user_id = any(${`{${aged.user.id},${off.user.id}}`}::uuid[])`);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_KINDS, ORDER_RULES, renderAlert, type AlertFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { StaffMessage } from "../../src/auth";

import { ageMessageForTest, closeNotifyFixtures, contactMessageForTest, nextValidity, outboxOf, outboxSince, removeMessages, type OutboxRow } from "./notify-fixtures";
import { newStaffKey, newStaffSession, rolledBack } from "./staff-fixtures";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 60_000 });

const MIN = 60_000;

/**
 * The alert channel's time-driven alerts and its two legs (3f design, sections 6.1, 7.2 and 12.1; invariants 14 and 15):
 * alert_steps() writes an escalation at escalate_minutes and the deadline's two reminders, each once, and stops them when
 * the message is handled; a person already at work in the console is not absent; the daily test is written once a day.
 * The alert tick mails every row whose mail is its sentence once, never one of 3c's or 3e's kinds, and with NOTIFY on
 * judges the channel's health with its own alarms, once in 24 hours. staffAlert writes the row of every kind of 3c and
 * 3e and marks it mailed either way.
 *
 * The steps run inside transactions of the migrator that end in a rollback: there the test sets the times it needs and
 * pushes every staff session back a day, so that the sessions earlier files of the run opened do not count as someone at
 * work. The tick commits, as the server's does; its rows and messages are removed by id, and the file's last test holds
 * it to leaving no row behind.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: the alert steps and the alert tick", () => {
  let w: NoticesWorld;
  let staffEmail: string;
  let before: Record<string, number>;
  const made: string[] = [];

    w = noticesWorld();

  afterAll(async () => {
    await w.migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.notify_state`);
    await closeNotifyFixtures();
    await w.close();
  });

  /** A message inside the migrator's transaction, received `minutes` ago: the migrator keeps the time it supplies. */
  const messageIn = async (tx: DbTx, minutes: number, extra: { stale?: boolean } = {}) => {
    const [row] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
      insert into public.contact_messages (folder, uidvalidity, uid, received_at, seen_at, stale)
      values ('inbox', ${nextValidity()}, 1, now() - make_interval(mins => ${minutes}), now() - make_interval(mins => ${minutes}), ${extra.stale ?? false}) returning id`);
    return row!.id;

  /** Every staff session pushed a day back, its lifetime with it: nobody is at work in the console. */
  const nobodyAtWork = (tx: DbTx) =>

  const steps = async (tx: DbTx) => Number((await tx.execute<{ written: number }>(sql`select public.alert_steps() as written`))[0]!.written);

  test("an unanswered message is escalated to every phone once, escalate_minutes after it arrived, and not before", async () => {
```
