```ts
      const live = and(
        eq(staffSessions.id, id),
        isNull(staffSessions.revokedAt),
        lte(staffSessions.createdAt, now),
        gt(staffSessions.idleExpiresAt, now),
        gt(staffSessions.absoluteExpiresAt, now),
        isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt),
        isNull(users.deletedAt),
        ne(users.role, "user"),
      );
      const columns = {
        id: staffSessions.id,
        handle: staffSessions.handle,
        userId: staffSessions.userId,
        keyId: staffSessions.keyId,
        role: users.role,
        createdAt: staffSessions.createdAt,
        lastUsedAt: staffSessions.lastUsedAt,
        idleExpiresAt: staffSessions.idleExpiresAt,
        absoluteExpiresAt: staffSessions.absoluteExpiresAt,
        browser: staffSessions.browser,
      };
      if (slideTo === null) {
        const [row] = await db
          .select(columns)
          .from(staffSessions)
          .innerJoin(staffKeys, eq(staffKeys.id, staffSessions.keyId))
          .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, staffSessions.userId))
          .where(live)
          .limit(1);
        return row;
      }
      const [row] = await db
        .update(staffSessions)
        // least() on the row's own absolute end, so the idle end never passes it, as the table's check also requires.
        .set({ lastUsedAt: now, idleExpiresAt: sql`least(${slideTo.toISOString()}::timestamptz, ${staffSessions.absoluteExpiresAt})` })
        .from(staffKeys)
        // A join in UPDATE ... FROM cannot name the updated table, so the account is reached through the key, whose owner
        // the sessions' foreign key on (key_id, user_id) makes the session's account.
        .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, staffKeys.userId))
        .where(and(eq(staffKeys.id, staffSessions.keyId), live))
        .returning(columns);
      return row;
    },

    /** The account's live staff sessions, the same tests as resolveStaffSession's, most recently used first. */
    async listStaffSessions(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<{ handle: string; browser: string; createdAt: Date; lastUsedAt: Date }[]> {
      return db
        .select({ handle: staffSessions.handle, browser: staffSessions.browser, createdAt: staffSessions.createdAt, lastUsedAt: staffSessions.lastUsedAt })
        .from(staffSessions)
        .innerJoin(staffKeys, eq(staffKeys.id, staffSessions.keyId))
        .where(
          and(
            eq(staffSessions.userId, userId),
            isNull(staffSessions.revokedAt),
            lte(staffSessions.createdAt, now),
            gt(staffSessions.idleExpiresAt, now),
            gt(staffSessions.absoluteExpiresAt, now),
            isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt),
          ),
        )
        .orderBy(desc(staffSessions.lastUsedAt), desc(staffSessions.createdAt));
    },

    /** The account's live staff keys as the console lists them, oldest first: never a public key, a credential id or an AAGUID. */
    async listStaffKeyViews(userId: string): Promise<{ id: string; name: string; createdAt: Date; lastUsedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      return db
        .select({ id: staffKeys.id, name: staffKeys.name, createdAt: staffKeys.createdAt, lastUsedAt: staffKeys.lastUsedAt })
        .from(staffKeys)
        .where(and(eq(staffKeys.userId, userId), isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt)))
        .orderBy(asc(staffKeys.createdAt), asc(staffKeys.id));
    },

    /**
     * A sign-out (3a design, section 7) in one transaction: the session revoked, if it still is live, then its
     * staff_signed_out event and last its audit row. False when another request ended it first, which writes nothing.
     */
    async endStaffSession(input: { id: string; userId: string; keyId: string; now: Date; ipHash: string | null; requestId: string }): Promise<boolean> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const [ended] = await tx
          .update(staffSessions)
          .set({ revokedAt: input.now })
          .where(and(eq(staffSessions.id, input.id), eq(staffSessions.userId, input.userId), isNull(staffSessions.revokedAt)))
          .returning({ handle: staffSessions.handle });
        if (!ended) return false;
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId: input.userId, type: "staff_signed_out", ipHash: input.ipHash, metadata: { handle: ended.handle } });
        await appendAudit(tx, {
          actorId: input.userId,
          action: "staff_signed_out",
          targetType: "staff_session",
          targetId: ended.handle,
          staffSession: ended.handle,
          keyId: input.keyId,
          metadata: {},
          requestId: input.requestId,
        });
        return true;
      });
    },

    /** The staff key a step-up confirms with, revoked or not, by its id; the step-up decides. */
    async findStaffKeyCredential(id: string): Promise<StaffKeyCredential | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select({
          id: staffKeys.id,
          userId: staffKeys.userId,
          credentialId: staffKeys.credentialId,
          publicKey: staffKeys.publicKey,
          transports: staffKeys.transports,
          name: staffKeys.name,
          revokedAt: staffKeys.revokedAt,
          origin: staffKeys.origin,
          rpId: staffKeys.rpId,
        })
        .from(staffKeys)
        .where(eq(staffKeys.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /**
     * The counter rule at a step-up (3a design, section 7), as at sign-in: the key's use is recorded only while it is live
     * and its counter moved forward. False when the update matched no row: a counter that went backwards, or a key
     * revoked since the step-up read it, which the caller hands to the counter rule's revocation.
     */
    async recordStaffKeyUse(input: { keyId: string; userId: string; newCounter: number; now: Date }): Promise<boolean> {
      return recordStaffKeyUse(db, input);
    },

    /**
     * Revokes one of the account's own live staff sessions, confirmed by a step-up, in one transaction on the auth role
     * (3a design, section 7). The account's row is locked first, FOR NO KEY UPDATE, as every revocation takes it, so a
     * revocation of the confirming key, a demotion or a take-down either committed before (and this refuses: the session
     * that confirmed has ended) or waits until this commits. Then the session, only where revoked_at is still null and
     * before both its ends, and only if it is the account's own; its staff_session_revoked event; and last its audit row,
     * through auth.append_audit, with the action's hash, its params in the metadata, the key and the assertion, which
     * audit-verify checks. "ended" when the confirming key or account no longer opens anything, "not_found" when the
     * handle names no live session of the account; neither writes anything.
     *
     * audit-verify refuses for good a row stamped at or after its challenge's expiry, and the trigger stamps the row only
     * once it holds the audit head, so a head held open would otherwise let a genuine confirmation become such a row. Every
     * lock wait here is therefore bounded by a third of the challenge's life left by the database's clock (at most 15
     * seconds), and the statement that writes the row also checks the database's clock against the expiry: "late" when a
     * wait gave up or the expiry came first, which rolls everything back and writes nothing.
     */
    async revokeConfirmedStaffSession(input: ConfirmedStaffSessionRevocation): Promise<"revoked" | "ended" | "not_found" | "late"> {
      try {
        return await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
          // Three waits: the account's row, the session's row and the audit head.
          if (!(await boundLockWaits(tx, input.expiresAt, 3))) return "late";
          return revokeConfirmedIn(tx, input);
        });
      } catch (err) {
        if (err instanceof LateConfirmation || isBoundReached(err)) return "late";
        throw err;
      }
    },

    /**
     * Revokes staff keys in one transaction on the auth role (3a design, section 7): `staff.js revoke <email> <key id>` and
     * `revoke <email> all`, and the counter rule's revocation, which is the same routine with suspect_at set as well and the
     * regression's own event. The account's row is locked first, FOR NO KEY UPDATE, as every writer of staff rows takes it.
     * Then the keys (one, or every live one), each only where revoked_at is still null, since a set one is never changed;
     * then every staff session they opened (for `all`, every staff session of the account), after the keys, so a session a
     * sign-in opened while this waited for a key's row is found too; for `all`, the unused enrolment links; an event per key;
     * and last the audit rows, a key's revocation each and, when a link went, one staff_enrollments_cancelled row, so it
     * never changes the database without a row. The command line waits at most 10 seconds for a lock.
     */
    async revokeStaffKeys(input: StaffKeyRevocation): Promise<StaffKeysRevoked> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx): Promise<StaffKeysRevoked> => {
        if (input.via === "cli") await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        const [account] = await tx
          .select({ id: users.id, email: users.email })
          .from(users)
          .where(and("id" in input.account ? eq(users.id, input.account.id) : sql`lower(${users.email}) = lower(${input.account.email})`, isNull(users.deletedAt)))
          .limit(1)
          .for("no key update");
        if (!account) return { ok: false, reason: "no_account" };
        let alreadyRevokedAt: Date | null = null;
        if (input.key !== "all") {
          // Another account's key and an unknown one are alike: neither is this account's to revoke.
          const [key] = await tx
            .select({ revokedAt: staffKeys.revokedAt })
            .from(staffKeys)
            .where(and(eq(staffKeys.id, input.key), eq(staffKeys.userId, account.id)));
          if (!key) return { ok: false, reason: "no_key" };
          alreadyRevokedAt = key.revokedAt;
        }
        const revoked = await tx
          .update(staffKeys)
          .set(input.suspect ? { revokedAt: input.now, suspectAt: input.now } : { revokedAt: input.now })
          .where(and(eq(staffKeys.userId, account.id), input.key === "all" ? undefined : eq(staffKeys.id, input.key), isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt)))
          .returning({ id: staffKeys.id, name: staffKeys.name, createdAt: staffKeys.createdAt });
        // An update answers in no set order; the events, rows and mail list the keys oldest first.
        revoked.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime() || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
        const keyIds = revoked.map((key) => key.id);
        const sessionsOf = input.key === "all" ? eq(staffSessions.userId, account.id) : keyIds.length > 0 ? inArray(staffSessions.keyId, keyIds) : null;
        const ended =
          sessionsOf === null
            ? []
            : await tx
                .update(staffSessions)
                .set({ revokedAt: input.now })
                .where(and(sessionsOf, isNull(staffSessions.revokedAt)))
                .returning({ keyId: staffSessions.keyId });
        const enrollmentsCancelled =
          input.key === "all"
            ? (
                await tx
                  .delete(staffEnrollments)
                  .where(and(eq(staffEnrollments.userId, account.id), isNull(staffEnrollments.usedAt)))
                  .returning({ id: staffEnrollments.id })
              ).length
            : 0;
        const action = input.suspect ? "staff_key_counter_regression" : "staff_key_revoked";
        const keys = revoked.map((key) => ({ id: key.id, name: key.name, sessionsRevoked: ended.filter((session) => session.keyId === key.id).length }));
        for (const key of keys) {
          // The key's id and no name: the take-down blanks names, and nothing can blank them in an event.
          await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId: account.id, type: action, metadata: { keyId: key.id, sessionsRevoked: key.sessionsRevoked, via: input.via } });
        }
        for (const key of keys) {
          await appendAudit(tx, {
            actorId: input.actorId,
            action,
            targetType: "staff_key",
            targetId: key.id,
            metadata: { keyId: key.id, sessionsRevoked: key.sessionsRevoked, via: input.via },
            requestId: input.requestId ?? null,
          });
        }
        if (enrollmentsCancelled > 0) {
          await appendAudit(tx, {
            actorId: input.actorId,
            action: "staff_enrollments_cancelled",
            targetType: "user",
            targetId: account.id,
            metadata: { count: enrollmentsCancelled, via: input.via },
            requestId: input.requestId ?? null,
          });
        }
        return { ok: true, userId: account.id, email: account.email, keys, staffSessionsRevoked: ended.length, enrollmentsCancelled, alreadyRevokedAt };
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ notifiers (3c design, section 6.1)

    /**
     * Stores what a signed-out notifier gave to be told about their notice, already encrypted, under the id the
     * moderation module chose and wrote on the notice. The role may never update any of it but the day it is forgotten.
     */
    async createNotifierContact(input: { id: string; nameEnc: string | null; emailEnc: string | null; emailHash: string | null; mailTokenEnc: string | null; forgetAfter: Date }): Promise<void> {
      await db.insert(notifierContacts).values(input);
    },

    async findNotifierContact(id: string): Promise<NotifierContactRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db.select().from(notifierContacts).where(eq(notifierContacts.id, id)).limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** What is known of these contacts without opening a ciphertext: whether a name and an address were given, and the address's hash. */
    async notifierContactFacts(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<{ id: string; named: boolean; contactGiven: boolean; emailHash: string | null }[]> {
      if (ids.length === 0) return [];
      return db
        .select({ id: notifierContacts.id, named: sql<boolean>`${notifierContacts.nameEnc} is not null`, contactGiven: sql<boolean>`${notifierContacts.emailEnc} is not null`, emailHash: notifierContacts.emailHash })
        .from(notifierContacts)
        .where(inArray(notifierContacts.id, [...ids]));
    },

    /** The contacts that gave this address, oldest first: the command line's read for an access request. */
    async notifierContactsByEmailHash(emailHash: string): Promise<NotifierContactRow[]> {
      return db.select().from(notifierContacts).where(eq(notifierContacts.emailHash, emailHash)).orderBy(asc(notifierContacts.createdAt), asc(notifierContacts.id));
    },

    /** Which of these address hashes hold a confirmation that has not run out. */
    async confirmedNotifierHashes(hashes: readonly string[], now: Date): Promise<Set<string>> {
      if (hashes.length === 0) return new Set();
      const rows = await db
        .select({ emailHash: notifierConfirmations.emailHash })
        .from(notifierConfirmations)
        .where(and(inArray(notifierConfirmations.emailHash, [...hashes]), gt(notifierConfirmations.expiresAt, now)));
      return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.emailHash));
    },

    /** Which of these address hashes asked korbat to stop its report mails. */
    async suppressedNotifierHashes(hashes: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
      if (hashes.length === 0) return new Set();
      const rows = await db.select({ emailHash: notifierSuppressions.emailHash }).from(notifierSuppressions).where(inArray(notifierSuppressions.emailHash, [...hashes]));
      return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.emailHash));
    },

    /**
     * Records an address as confirmed until `expiresAt` and lifts any stop of it, in one transaction: whoever holds a
     * mail korbat sent there said "I sent this", which also means they want its mails.
     */
    async confirmNotifierAddress(emailHash: string, now: Date, expiresAt: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx
          .insert(notifierConfirmations)
          .values({ emailHash, confirmedAt: now, expiresAt })
          .onConflictDoUpdate({ target: notifierConfirmations.emailHash, set: { confirmedAt: now, expiresAt } });
        await tx.delete(notifierSuppressions).where(eq(notifierSuppressions.emailHash, emailHash));
      });
    },

    /** Records that an address asked korbat to stop its report mails; a second stop changes nothing. The role cannot update the row. */
    async suppressNotifierAddress(emailHash: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.insert(notifierSuppressions).values({ emailHash }).onConflictDoNothing();
    },

    /** Lifts a stop; true when there was one. */
    async liftNotifierSuppression(emailHash: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db.delete(notifierSuppressions).where(eq(notifierSuppressions.emailHash, emailHash)).returning({ emailHash: notifierSuppressions.emailHash });
      return rows.length > 0;
    },

    /** Moves the day these contacts are forgotten: the one column of a contact the role may update. */
    async setNotifierForgetAfter(ids: readonly string[], at: Date): Promise<void> {
      if (ids.length === 0) return;
      await db.update(notifierContacts).set({ forgetAfter: at }).where(inArray(notifierContacts.id, [...ids]));
    },

    /** How many contacts were to be forgotten, and confirmations had run out, before `before`: what a janitor that ran would have removed. */
    async countNotifierRowsDue(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(
        sql`select (select count(*) from auth.notifier_contacts where forget_after < ${before.toISOString()}::timestamptz)
                 + (select count(*) from auth.notifier_confirmations where expires_at < ${before.toISOString()}::timestamptz) as due`,
      )) as unknown as { due: string | number }[];
      return Number(row?.due ?? 0);
    },

    /** The address of every live staff account: not deleted, and a moderator or an admin. */
    async liveStaffAddresses(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ email: users.email })
        .from(users)
        .where(and(isNull(users.deletedAt), ne(users.role, "user")))
        .orderBy(asc(users.createdAt), asc(users.id));
      return rows.map((row) => row.email);
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ events

    async appendEvent(input: {
      userId: string | null;
      type: AuthEventType;
      deviceId?: string | null;
      ipHash?: string | null;
      metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
    }): Promise<void> {
      await db.insert(authEvents).values({
        userId: input.userId,
        type: input.type,
        deviceId: input.deviceId ?? null,
        ipHash: input.ipHash ?? null,
        metadata: input.metadata ?? {},
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ retention

    /** Codes consumed or expired before `before` are of no use to anyone; they still hold an email and an ip hash. */
    async purgeEmailCodes(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .delete(emailCodes)
        .where(or(and(sql`${emailCodes.consumedAt} is not null`, lt(emailCodes.consumedAt, before)), lt(emailCodes.expiresAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: emailCodes.id });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /** Sessions revoked or expired before `before`. Live ones are never touched. */
    async purgeSessions(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .delete(sessions)
        .where(or(and(sql`${sessions.revokedAt} is not null`, lt(sessions.revokedAt, before)), lt(sessions.expiresAt, before), lt(sessions.absoluteExpiresAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: sessions.id });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /**
     * Staff sessions revoked or expired before `before` (3a design, section 7). A live one is never touched: both its ends
     * lie ahead. The audit rows that name a session keep its handle, which needs no row.
     */
    async purgeStaffSessions(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .delete(staffSessions)
        .where(
          or(
            and(isNotNull(staffSessions.revokedAt), lt(staffSessions.revokedAt, before)),
            lt(staffSessions.idleExpiresAt, before),
            lt(staffSessions.absoluteExpiresAt, before),
          ),
        )
        .returning({ id: staffSessions.id });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /** Enrolment links used or expired before `before`, which can enrol nothing more; one that still can is cancelled only by name. */
    async purgeStaffEnrollments(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .delete(staffEnrollments)
        .where(or(and(isNotNull(staffEnrollments.usedAt), lt(staffEnrollments.usedAt, before)), lt(staffEnrollments.expiresAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: staffEnrollments.id });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /** The design's IP-hash purge: a device not seen since `before` keeps no address hash. */
    async purgeDeviceIpHashes(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(devices)
        .set({ ipHash: null })
        .where(and(sql`${devices.ipHash} is not null`, lt(devices.lastSeenAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: devices.id });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /** Notifier contacts whose day to be forgotten lies before `before` (3c design, section 6.1): the name, the address and the mail token go with the row. */
    async purgeNotifierContacts(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db.delete(notifierContacts).where(lt(notifierContacts.forgetAfter, before)).returning({ id: notifierContacts.id });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /** Confirmations of a notifier's address that ran out before `before`: an address is confirmed for 30 days. */
    async purgeNotifierConfirmations(before: Date): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db.delete(notifierConfirmations).where(lt(notifierConfirmations.expiresAt, before)).returning({ emailHash: notifierConfirmations.emailHash });
      return rows.length;
    },

    /**
     * Events older than `days` days, through auth.purge_events (migration 0007): the table stays
     * append-only for this role, which holds no DELETE on it; the function is owned by the migrator.
     */
    async purgeEvents(days: number): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`select auth.purge_events(make_interval(days => ${days}::int)) as removed`)) as unknown as { removed: number }[];
      return Number(row?.removed ?? 0);
    },

    async recentEvents(userId: string, limit = 20) {
      return db
        .select({ type: authEvents.type, deviceId: authEvents.deviceId, createdAt: authEvents.createdAt })
        .from(authEvents)
        .where(eq(authEvents.userId, userId))
        .orderBy(desc(authEvents.createdAt), desc(authEvents.id))
        .limit(limit);
    },

    /** The user's own events since `since`, newest first, for the data export: their kind and time, never the metadata. */
    async eventsSince(userId: string, since: Date): Promise<{ type: AuthEventType; createdAt: Date }[]> {
      return db
        .select({ type: authEvents.type, createdAt: authEvents.createdAt })
        .from(authEvents)
        .where(and(eq(authEvents.userId, userId), gte(authEvents.createdAt, since)))
        .orderBy(desc(authEvents.createdAt), desc(authEvents.id));
    },
  };
}

type Tx = Parameters<Parameters<Db["transaction"]>[0]>[0];
/** What a read runs through: the pool, or a transaction that needs the read to see its own lock. */
type Querier = Pick<Db, "select">;

/** The auth side's actions in the audit log: the only ones auth.append_audit writes (migration 0012). */
type AuthAuditAction =
  | "staff_key_revoked"
  | "staff_key_counter_regression"
  | "staff_sign_in"
  | "staff_signed_out"
  | "staff_session_revoked"
  | "staff_enrollments_cancelled"
  | "role_granted";

/** One auth-side row of the audit log. The trigger sets its id, time, place and hashes. */
interface AuthAuditRow {
  actorId: string;
  action: AuthAuditAction;
  targetType: string | null;
  targetId: string | null;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
  staffSession?: string | null;
  keyId?: string | null;
  actionHash?: string | null;
  stepUp?: { authenticatorData: string; clientDataJSON: string; signature: string } | null;
  requestId?: string | null;
}

/**
 * Writes an auth-side row of the audit log in the caller's transaction, through auth.append_audit: the auth role holds
 * nothing in the public schema, and the function, which the migrator owns, writes only the auth side's actions (3a design,
 * section 6). It must be the transaction's last statement: the row holds the chain's head until the commit, so nothing that
 * can wait may run after it. Answers the row's place in the chain.
 */
async function appendAudit(tx: Tx, row: AuthAuditRow): Promise<number> {
  // The jsonb arguments go as text and are cast, so postgres.js sends them exactly as serialised here.
  const stepUp = row.stepUp ? JSON.stringify(row.stepUp) : null;
  const [written] = await tx.execute<{ place: string }>(
    sql`select auth.append_audit(${row.actorId}::uuid, ${row.action}::text, ${row.targetType}::text, ${row.targetId}::text,
      ${JSON.stringify(row.metadata)}::text::jsonb, ${row.staffSession ?? null}::uuid, ${row.keyId ?? null}::uuid,
      ${row.actionHash ?? null}::text, ${stepUp}::text::jsonb, ${row.requestId ?? null}::text)::text as place`,
  );
  return Number(written!.place);
}

/**
 * A confirmed action whose row could not join the chain before its step-up challenge expired; nothing was written.
 * Exported for the step-up suite, which runs revokeConfirmedIn past its challenge's expiry and expects this.
 */
export class LateConfirmation extends Error {
  constructor() {
    super("the confirmation's row could not join the chain before its challenge expired");
    this.name = "LateConfirmation";
  }
}

/**
 * appendAudit for a row a step-up confirmed, in one statement that also reads the database's clock once the row is in the
 * chain: the trigger stamped the row no later than that, so a clock still before the challenge's expiry means the row is
 * too, as audit-verify requires. The audit row stays the last statement of its transaction. False when the expiry came
 * first: the caller then rolls the transaction back.
 */
async function appendAuditBefore(tx: Tx, expiresAt: Date, row: AuthAuditRow): Promise<boolean> {
  const stepUp = row.stepUp ? JSON.stringify(row.stepUp) : null;
  // A volatile function in a CTE is evaluated once, before the outer query reads its row, so the clock is read after it.
  const [written] = await tx.execute<{ inTime: boolean }>(
    sql`with written as (
      select auth.append_audit(${row.actorId}::uuid, ${row.action}::text, ${row.targetType}::text, ${row.targetId}::text,
        ${JSON.stringify(row.metadata)}::text::jsonb, ${row.staffSession ?? null}::uuid, ${row.keyId ?? null}::uuid,
        ${row.actionHash ?? null}::text, ${stepUp}::text::jsonb, ${row.requestId ?? null}::text) as place
    )
    select extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000 < ${expiresAt.getTime()}::numeric as "inTime" from written`,
  );
  return written!.inTime === true;
}

/**
 * revokeConfirmedStaffSession's statements, in its transaction: the account's row first, then the key, the session, the
 * event, and last the audit row, written only while the challenge has not expired by the database's clock.
 *
 * Exported for the step-up suite alone, which runs it without boundLockWaits on a challenge already expired, as if the
 * waits had together outlasted it: that is the only way to reach the row's own clock check on cue, since the bound ends
 * any one wait the suite could hold before then. Everything else calls revokeConfirmedStaffSession.
 */
export async function revokeConfirmedIn(tx: Tx, input: ConfirmedStaffSessionRevocation): Promise<"revoked" | "ended" | "not_found"> {
  const [account] = await tx
    .select({ id: users.id })
    .from(users)
    .where(and(eq(users.id, input.userId), isNull(users.deletedAt), ne(users.role, "user")))
    .limit(1)
    .for("no key update");
  if (!account) return "ended";
  const [key] = await tx
    .select({ id: staffKeys.id })
    .from(staffKeys)
    .where(and(eq(staffKeys.id, input.keyId), eq(staffKeys.userId, input.userId), isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt)));
  if (!key) return "ended";
  const [revoked] = await tx
    .update(staffSessions)
    .set({ revokedAt: input.now })
    .where(
      and(
        eq(staffSessions.handle, input.handle),
        eq(staffSessions.userId, input.userId),
        isNull(staffSessions.revokedAt),
        gt(staffSessions.idleExpiresAt, input.now),
        gt(staffSessions.absoluteExpiresAt, input.now),
      ),
    )
    .returning({ handle: staffSessions.handle });
  if (!revoked) return "not_found";
  // The account's own log names the session that ended and the one that ended it.
  await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId: input.userId, type: "staff_session_revoked", ipHash: input.ipHash, metadata: { handle: revoked.handle, by: input.staffSession } });
  const inTime = await appendAuditBefore(tx, input.expiresAt, {
    actorId: input.userId,
    action: "staff_session_revoked",
    targetType: "staff_session",
    targetId: revoked.handle,
    staffSession: input.staffSession,
    keyId: input.keyId,
    actionHash: input.actionHash,
    stepUp: input.stepUp,
    metadata: { params: input.params },
    requestId: input.requestId,
  });
  // Thrown, so the transaction rolls back: the session stays live and no row is written.
  if (!inTime) throw new LateConfirmation();
  return "revoked";
}

/**
 * 1c's counter rule as one conditional update of a staff key (3a design, section 7), at a sign-in in the session's
 * transaction and at a step-up on its own: the key's use and counter are recorded only while it is the account's, live, and
 * its counter moved forward (two zeros pass, as some authenticators always report 0). False when no row matched. The
 * update holds the key's row until the commit, so a revocation waiting for it then also finds what this transaction did.
 */
async function recordStaffKeyUse(q: Pick<Db, "update">, input: { keyId: string; userId: string; newCounter: number; now: Date }): Promise<boolean> {
  const claimed = await q
    .update(staffKeys)
    .set({ counter: input.newCounter, lastUsedAt: input.now })
    .where(
      and(
        eq(staffKeys.id, input.keyId),
        eq(staffKeys.userId, input.userId),
        isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt),
        sql`((${input.newCounter} = 0 and ${staffKeys.counter} = 0) or ${input.newCounter} > ${staffKeys.counter})`,
      ),
    )
    .returning({ id: staffKeys.id });
  return claimed.length > 0;
}

/**
 * The daily bound's reading (1c design, section 2): how many passkey_added events the account has within the window, at
 * most `limit` of them, and the seconds until the oldest of those is out of the window, when the day has a slot again.
 * Counted from the events, so a removal frees nothing, and by the database clock, which wrote them.
 */
async function recentPasskeyAdditions(q: Querier, userId: string, withinMs: number, limit: number): Promise<{ count: number; retryAfterSeconds: number }> {
  const window = sql`make_interval(secs => ${withinMs / 1000}::float8)`;
  const recent = q
    .select({ createdAt: authEvents.createdAt })
    .from(authEvents)
    .where(and(eq(authEvents.userId, userId), eq(authEvents.type, "passkey_added"), gt(authEvents.createdAt, sql`now() - ${window}`)))
    .orderBy(desc(authEvents.createdAt))
    .limit(limit)
    .as("recent");
  const [row] = await q
    .select({
      count: sql<number>`count(*)::int`,
      retryAfterSeconds: sql<number>`coalesce(ceil(extract(epoch from (min(${recent.createdAt}) + ${window} - now())))::int, 0)`,
    })
    .from(recent);
  return { count: row?.count ?? 0, retryAfterSeconds: row?.retryAfterSeconds ?? 0 };
}

/** The message of an exception a PL/pgSQL function raised (SQLSTATE P0001), however deeply the driver wrapped it; null for anything else. */
function raisedMessage(err: unknown): string | null {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    if (typeof current === "object" && (current as { code?: unknown }).code === "P0001") {
      const message = (current as { message?: unknown }).message;
      return typeof message === "string" ? message : null;
    }
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return null;
}

/** What revoking an account's staff access did, for the auth events already written, the audit rows and the mail. */
interface StaffRevocation {
  /** Each key revoked now, oldest first, with how many of its staff sessions were revoked now. */
  keys: { id: string; name: string; sessionsRevoked: number }[];
  staffSessionsRevoked: number;
  /**
   * The open enrolment links (never used) deleted now: the deletions that end something, and the count the record carries.
   * A spent link deleted with them at a take-down is not counted, since it could enrol nothing more and nothing was cancelled.
   */
  enrollmentsCancelled: number;
}

/**
 * Ends an account's staff access inside the caller's transaction, which has locked the account's row first (3a design,
 * section 7): when `keys` is set every live staff key is revoked, then every staff session not yet revoked, the
 * enrolment links deleted (the unused ones, or every one at a take-down), and a staff_key_revoked event for each key. The
 * keys go before the sessions, as in revokeStaffKeys: a sign-in holds its key's row from the moment it records the key's
 * use until it commits the session it opens, and the session's insert does not wait for the account's lock, so a session
 * opened while this waited for a key's row is committed by the time the sessions are revoked, and is found and counted.
 * A revocation sets revoked_at only where it is still null, since a set one is never changed. Writes no audit row: the
 * caller writes those last, after its own statements.
 */
async function revokeStaffAccess(
  tx: Tx,
  userId: string,
  now: Date,
  options: { keys: boolean; enrollments: "unused" | "all"; via: "role_change" | "take_down" },
): Promise<StaffRevocation> {
  const revoked = options.keys
    ? await tx
        .update(staffKeys)
        .set({ revokedAt: now })
        .where(and(eq(staffKeys.userId, userId), isNull(staffKeys.revokedAt)))
        .returning({ id: staffKeys.id, name: staffKeys.name, createdAt: staffKeys.createdAt })
    : [];
  const ended = await tx
    .update(staffSessions)
    .set({ revokedAt: now })
    .where(and(eq(staffSessions.userId, userId), isNull(staffSessions.revokedAt)))
    .returning({ keyId: staffSessions.keyId });
  const deleted = await tx
    .delete(staffEnrollments)
    .where(and(eq(staffEnrollments.userId, userId), options.enrollments === "unused" ? isNull(staffEnrollments.usedAt) : undefined))
    .returning({ usedAt: staffEnrollments.usedAt });
  const keys: StaffRevocation["keys"] = [];
  if (options.keys) {
    // An update answers in no set order; the events, rows and mail list the keys oldest first.
    revoked.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt.getTime() - b.createdAt.getTime() || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
    for (const key of revoked) {
      const sessionsRevoked = ended.filter((session) => session.keyId === key.id).length;
      keys.push({ id: key.id, name: key.name, sessionsRevoked });
      // The key's id and no name: the take-down blanks names, and nothing can blank them in an event.
      await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId, type: "staff_key_revoked", metadata: { keyId: key.id, sessionsRevoked, via: options.via } });
    }
  }
  return { keys, staffSessionsRevoked: ended.length, enrollmentsCancelled: deleted.filter((link) => link.usedAt === null).length };
}

/** The audit row of each staff key a revocation revoked, in the order of its events; among the caller's last statements. */
async function appendKeyRevocations(tx: Tx, actorId: string, revocation: StaffRevocation, via: "role_change" | "take_down"): Promise<void> {
  for (const key of revocation.keys) {
    await appendAudit(tx, {
      actorId,
      action: "staff_key_revoked",
      targetType: "staff_key",
      targetId: key.id,
      metadata: { keyId: key.id, sessionsRevoked: key.sessionsRevoked, via },
    });
  }
}

/**
 * A take-down's audit rows, its transaction's last statements (3a design, section 7): each staff key's revocation and,
 * when an open enrolment link went, one staff_enrollments_cancelled row with their count, so the take-down never ends
 * any staff access without a row on the record. The spent links it deletes too are no cancellation, and like the
 * janitor's deletions of them they get no row. Nothing when the account had no staff access left to take.
 */
async function appendTakeDownAudit(tx: Tx, actorId: string, userId: string, revocation: StaffRevocation): Promise<void> {
  await appendKeyRevocations(tx, actorId, revocation, "take_down");
  if (revocation.enrollmentsCancelled > 0) {
    await appendAudit(tx, {
      actorId,
      action: "staff_enrollments_cancelled",
      targetType: "user",
      targetId: userId,
      metadata: { count: revocation.enrollmentsCancelled, via: "take_down" },
    });
  }
}

/**
 * The rows step 1 of a deletion takes down, inside the caller's transaction: every live session is revoked
 * (its id answered, for the cache tombstones), every device is deleted, and with it by cascade every session
 * row, every code out for the user goes, whatever its purpose, so none can complete a flow for an account
 * that is gone, and every passkey goes with the WebAuthn user handle (1c design, section 7.7), so a deleted
 * account keeps no credential of any kind and no assertion can name it again. Its staff access ends too (3a design,
 * section 7): its live staff keys and staff sessions are revoked, with a staff_key_revoked event per key, and its
 * enrolment links deleted. The keys themselves are never deleted, since audit-verify checks old confirmations against
 * them, so auth.forget_staff_keys blanks their names, AAGUIDs and transports and keeps what audit-verify needs. It writes
 * no audit row: the caller writes those last, from what this answers. Run again by finishTakeDown, each statement finds
 * nothing more to do.
 */
async function takeDownRows(tx: Tx, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<{ sessionIds: string[]; staff: StaffRevocation }> {
  const revoked = await tx
    .update(sessions)
    .set({ revokedAt: now })
    .where(and(eq(sessions.userId, userId), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
    .returning({ id: sessions.id });
  await tx.delete(devices).where(eq(devices.userId, userId));
  await tx.delete(emailCodes).where(eq(emailCodes.userId, userId));
  await tx.delete(passkeys).where(eq(passkeys.userId, userId));
  // The handle only ever named the account to its passkeys and staff keys; cleared here rather than by finishPurge, so the
  // take-down leaves nothing of the ceremony behind.
  await tx.update(users).set({ webauthnUserId: null }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
  const staff = await revokeStaffAccess(tx, userId, now, { keys: true, enrollments: "all", via: "take_down" });
  // The account is marked deleted by now, which the function checks: for a live account it would change nothing.
  await tx.execute(sql`select auth.forget_staff_keys(${userId}::uuid)`);
  return { sessionIds: revoked.map((row) => row.id), staff };
}

export type AuthRepo = ReturnType<typeof createAuthRepo>;
```

```ts
/**
 * The staff command line's commands for authorities' orders (3f design, section 8.11, "Orders"; section 7.7): what only
 * the operator records, which the console cannot take. staff.ts reads their settings and opens their connection, as the
 * migrator, in the migrate service; this file parses their arguments and does what each does. Every command is one
 * transaction with the 10-second lock timeout, takes the order's row FOR UPDATE, writes its change and its event (via
 * `cli`), and ends with the audit row `order_recorded` (the system actor; target the order; metadata the event and its
 * facts, a text only as its digest). Every line it prints starts with its name, and a refusal is one sentence ending in
 * "nothing changed", exit 1. An instant is written with its offset: on the night the clocks go back a local time names
 * two instants.
 *
 * order-open writes the rows the console's route writes, through the moderation module's insertOrder, and before its
 * audit row the alert order_opened, which the watcher pushes and the alert tick mails: an order opened at the shell is
 * heard like any other. Task 3: order-texts tells the authors of the order's told notices that a notice grew (the mail
 * order_notice_added, sent by the dispatch round), and the hold's commands move or end an order's hold.
 *
 * This file has no entry point of its own, so both bundles can include it (build.mjs says why that matters).
 */

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import {

  FORBIDDEN_FORMAT,

} from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../auth";
import { preservedImages } from "../media";
import { insertOrder, orderItemsFor } from "../moderation";
import { appendAuditRow } from "../staff";

/** The order commands, each with its first line of STAFF_USAGE. */
export const ORDER_COMMANDS = [
  "order-open",
  "order-received",
  "order-sent-at",
  "order-due",
  "order-verify",
  "order-issued",
  "order-texts",

  "order-scrutiny",

  "order-hold-until",

  // Task 4: the preservation's two commands (section 7.11); each names an order's item, not the order.
  "order-preserve-extend",
  "order-access",
] as const;
export type OrderCommandName = (typeof ORDER_COMMANDS)[number];

export const ORDER_USAGE = [
  "  order-open --kind <kind> --state <CC> --authority <text> --reference <text> --channel <mailbox|portal|post|other>",
  "             [--message <id>] [--received <instant>] [--sent <instant>] [--section-c] [--emergency] [--withhold] --link <url> ...",
  "                                         open an order whose time of receipt the console cannot take; run it in the migrate service",
  "  order-received <order> <instant>       the receipt of an order opened without a message",
  "  order-sent-at <order> <instant>        the sending time the channel states",
  "  order-due <order> <instant|none>       a DSA order's deadline as its text states it",
  "  order-verify <order> --how <text>      the check of the order against the register or the coordinator",
  "  order-issued <order> <instant> [--release]  the order's own date and time",
  "  order-texts <order> --reasons|--redress|--scope < text   the authority's words, read from standard input (run with -T)",
  "  order-document <order> < file          the document's SHA-256 and length; no byte of it is kept (run with -T)",
  "  order-scrutiny <order> requested --by <korbat|author> --at <instant> | decided --outcome <upheld|annulled> --at <instant>",
  "  order-reopen <order> --how <text>      open again an order that was closed by mistake or restored by a court",
  "  order-tell-rule <order> --when <at_effect|never|instant> --basis <text>   when the person an order to provide information names may be told",
  "  order-told <order> --at <instant> --how <text>   that the operator told that person",
  "  order-hold-until <order> <instant|none> --basis <text> --how <text> [--release]   the end of non-disclosure the authority stated",
  "  order-hold-extend <order> --received <instant> --how <text>   a removal order's one extension of non-disclosure, or the check of the console's",
  "  order-hold-end <order> --reason <not_authentic|annulled|released_by_authority|not_ordered> --how <text>   end a hold at once",
  "  order-preserve-extend <item> --until <instant> --by <text> --reference <text> --proceedings <text> --received <instant>",

  "  An <order> is its id, or <CC>:<reference> while one order of that state has the reference. An <item> is its id. Every instant has its offset.",
];

/** A parsed order command: its name, the order it names (none for order-open) and its flags and positional words. */
export interface OrderCommand {
  command: OrderCommandName;
  order: string | null;
  positional: string[];
  flags: Map<string, string[]>;
}

/** Flags that take no value. */
const SWITCHES = new Set(["--section-c", "--emergency", "--withhold", "--release", "--reasons", "--redress", "--scope"]);

/** Splits a command's words into its order, its positional words and its flags; a flag may repeat (--link). */
export function parseOrderArgs(command: OrderCommandName, rest: readonly string[]): OrderCommand {
  const flags = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const positional: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < rest.length; i++) {
    const word = rest[i]!;
    if (word.startsWith("--")) {
      if (SWITCHES.has(word)) {
        flags.set(word, [...(flags.get(word) ?? []), ""]);
        continue;
      }
      const value = rest[i + 1];
      if (value === undefined) throw new Error(`${command}: ${word} needs a value`);
      flags.set(word, [...(flags.get(word) ?? []), value]);
      i++;
    } else positional.push(word);
  }
  if (command === "order-open") return { command, order: null, positional, flags };
  const [order, ...others] = positional;
  // The preservation's commands name an order's item, which has no reference of its own: its id alone.
  if (order === undefined) throw new Error(command === "order-preserve-extend" || command === "order-access" ? `${command}: name the order's item by its id` : `${command}: name the order, by its id or as <CC>:<reference>`);
  return { command, order, positional: others, flags };
}

/** What a command reports: its lines, or its one sentence of refusal. */
export type OrderDone = { ok: true; lines: string[] } | { ok: false; problem: string };

/** The settings a command reads beside the migrator's URL: order-open needs both, order-tell-rule reads the home state. */
export interface OrderSettings {
  homeState: string | null;
  appOrigin: string | null;
}

/** A refusal: one sentence, then "nothing changed". Task 5: shared with cli/records.ts. */
export class Refusal extends Error {}
export const refuse = (command: string, why: string): never => {
  throw new Refusal(`${command}: ${why}; nothing changed`);
};

/** An instant with its offset (2026-10-10T01:00:12Z, 2026-10-10T03:00:12+02:00); a time without one names two on a night the clocks go back. */
const INSTANT = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2}([.][0-9]{1,6})?)?(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})$/;
export function instant(command: string, word: string | undefined): Date {
  if (word === undefined || !INSTANT.test(word) || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(word))) return refuse(command, `${word ?? "nothing"} is not an instant with an offset`);
  return new Date(word);
}

/** The one value of a flag, or a refusal naming it. */
export function flag(cmd: { command: string; flags: Map<string, string[]> }, name: string, required = true): string | null {
  const values = cmd.flags.get(name);
  if (values === undefined || values.length === 0) return required ? refuse(cmd.command, `${name} is required`) : null;
  if (values.length > 1) return refuse(cmd.command, `${name} is given more than once`);
  return values[0]!;
}

/** Whether a text holds a control character: C0, DEL or C1; `allowLineFeed` lets the line feed through. */
function hasControl(text: string, allowLineFeed: boolean): boolean {
  return [...text].some((char) => {
    const code = char.codePointAt(0)!;
    if (allowLineFeed && code === 10) return false;
    return code < 32 || (code >= 127 && code < 160);
  });
}

/** A free text of the command line (--how, --basis): about the act and never about the person, one line, at most 500 characters. */
export function freeText(command: string, name: string, text: string): string {
  if (!(text as string & { isWellFormed(): boolean }).isWellFormed() || hasControl(text, false) || FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text) || text.trim() === "") {
    return refuse(command, `${name} is one line of text without control or invisible characters`);
  }
  if (Array.from(text).length > ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.short) return refuse(command, `${name} has more than ${ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.short} characters`);
  return text;
}

/** An authority's name or a reference as the command line takes it (Task 5): under the contracts' rules for an order's. */
export function authorityText(command: string, name: string, text: string): string {
  const parsed = (name === "--authority" ? OrderAuthority : OrderReference).safeParse(text);
  return parsed.success ? parsed.data : refuse(command, `${name} is one line of 1 to 200 characters without control or invisible characters`);
}

export const sha256 = (data: string | Buffer) => createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex");
export const rows = async <T>(q: Db | DbTx, query: ReturnType<typeof sql>): Promise<T[]> => (await q.execute(query)) as unknown as T[];
export const isoOf = (expression: string) => sql.raw(`to_char(${expression} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')`);

/** The order a command names, by its id or as <CC>:<reference>; order_ambiguous when several orders of the state share the reference. */
export async function orderNamed(tx: DbTx, command: string, name: string): Promise<string> {
  if (/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/.test(name)) {
    const [found] = await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from public.legal_orders where id = ${name}::uuid`);
    return found?.id ?? refuse(command, `no order has the id ${name}`);
  }
  const at = name.indexOf(":");
  const state = name.slice(0, at);
  if (at < 0 || !/^[A-Z]{2}$/.test(state)) return refuse(command, `${name} is neither an order's id nor <CC>:<reference>`);
  const found = await rows<{ id: string; authority: string }>(
    tx,
    sql`select id, authority from public.legal_orders where member_state = ${state} and reference = ${name.slice(at + 1)} order by opened_at, id`,
  );
  if (found.length === 0) return refuse(command, `no order of ${state} has this reference`);
  if (found.length > 1) {
    throw new Refusal(
      [`order_ambiguous: ${found.length} orders of ${state} have this reference; name one by its id:`, ...found.map((row) => `  ${row.id} ${JSON.stringify(row.authority)}`), "nothing changed"].join(String.fromCharCode(10)),
    );
  }
  return found[0]!.id;
}

/** The facts of an order a command reads after its lock. */
interface Locked {
  id: string;
  kind: OrderKind;
  sectionC: boolean;
  receivedAt: string | null;
  sentAt: string | null;
  openedAt: string;
  closedAt: string | null;
  holdEndedAt: string | null;
  released: boolean;
  tellPerson: TellPersonRule | null;
  tellPersonAt: string | null;
}

/** The order's row FOR UPDATE, then what the command reads of it in a statement of its own. */
async function lockOrder(tx: DbTx, command: string, name: string): Promise<Locked> {
  const id = await orderNamed(tx, command, name);
  await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from public.legal_orders where id = ${id}::uuid for update`);
  const [row] = await rows<Record<string, unknown>>(
    tx,
    sql`select o.id, o.kind, o.section_c, ${isoOf("o.received_at")} as received_at, ${isoOf("o.sent_at")} as sent_at, ${isoOf("o.opened_at")} as opened_at,
               ${isoOf("o.closed_at")} as closed_at, ${isoOf("o.hold_ended_at")} as hold_ended_at, o.tell_person, ${isoOf("o.tell_person_at")} as tell_person_at,
               exists (select 1 from public.legal_order_events e where e.order_id = o.id and e.kind = 'notice_released') as released
          from public.legal_orders o where o.id = ${id}::uuid`,
  );
  return {
    id,
    kind: row!.kind as OrderKind,
    sectionC: row!.section_c as boolean,
    receivedAt: row!.received_at as string | null,
    sentAt: row!.sent_at as string | null,
    openedAt: row!.opened_at as string,
    closedAt: row!.closed_at as string | null,
    holdEndedAt: row!.hold_ended_at as string | null,
    released: row!.released as boolean,
    tellPerson: row!.tell_person as TellPersonRule | null,
    tellPersonAt: row!.tell_person_at as string | null,
  };
}

/** The event of a command, via the command line, then its audit row `order_recorded`, last. */
async function recorded(tx: DbTx, orderId: string, event: string, facts: Record<string, unknown>, columns: { ground?: string | null; effectiveAt?: Date | null } = {}): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`insert into public.legal_order_events (order_id, kind, ground, effective_at, via)
                       values (${orderId}::uuid, ${event}, ${columns.ground ?? null}, ${columns.effectiveAt?.toISOString() ?? null}::timestamptz, 'cli')`);
  await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "order_recorded", targetType: "order", targetId: orderId, requestId: null, metadata: { event, ...facts } });
}

/** The notice's hold of an order as order-issued prints it: "held until <instant>", "held with no end" or "not held". */
async function holdWords(tx: DbTx, orderId: string): Promise<string> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ until: string | null; infinite: boolean; ahead: boolean }>(
    tx,
    sql`select ${isoOf("h.until")} as until, coalesce(h.until = 'infinity'::timestamptz, false) as infinite, coalesce(h.until > clock_timestamp(), false) as ahead
          from (select public.order_hold_until(${orderId}::uuid) as until) h`,
  );
  if (row!.infinite) return "held with no end";
  return row!.until !== null && row!.ahead ? `held until ${row!.until}` : "not held";
}

/** A removal order's deadline from a start, as the console prints it. */
const deadlineOf = (start: string) => new Date(Date.parse(start) + ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes * 60_000).toISOString();

/** Runs one order command as the migrator, in one transaction with the 10-second lock timeout; a refusal changes nothing. */
export async function orderCommand(migrateDb: Db, cmd: OrderCommand, settings: OrderSettings, input: () => Promise<Buffer>): Promise<OrderDone> {
  // Standard input is read before the transaction opens: nothing holds a lock while a person types or a pipe drains.
  const stdin = cmd.command === "order-texts" || cmd.command === "order-document" ? await input() : null;
  try {
    const lines = await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
      return run(tx, cmd, settings, stdin);
    });
    return { ok: true, lines };
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof Refusal) return { ok: false, problem: err.message };
    throw err;
  }
}

async function run(tx: DbTx, cmd: OrderCommand, settings: OrderSettings, stdin: Buffer | null): Promise<string[]> {
  const c = cmd.command;
  switch (c) {
    case "order-open":
      return open(tx, cmd, settings);
    case "order-received": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const at = instant(c, cmd.positional[0]);
      if (order.receivedAt !== null) refuse(c, `the receipt is recorded already (${order.receivedAt})`);
      if (at.getTime() > Date.parse(order.openedAt)) refuse(c, "an order is not received after it was opened");
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set received_at = ${at.toISOString()}::timestamptz where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "received_set", { receivedAt: at.toISOString() });
      if (order.kind !== "tco_removal") return [`${c}: receipt ${at.toISOString()}.`];
      const start = order.sentAt !== null && Date.parse(order.sentAt) < at.getTime() ? order.sentAt : at.toISOString();
      const deadline = deadlineOf(start);
      const late = Math.floor((Date.now() - Date.parse(deadline)) / 60_000);
      return [late > 0 ? `${c}: receipt ${at.toISOString()}; deadline passed ${late} minutes ago.` : `${c}: receipt ${at.toISOString()}; deadline ${deadline}.`];
    }
    case "order-sent-at": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const at = instant(c, cmd.positional[0]);
      if (at.getTime() > Date.parse(order.openedAt)) refuse(c, "an order is not sent after it was opened");
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set sent_at = ${at.toISOString()}::timestamptz where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "sent_at_set", { sentAt: at.toISOString() });
      if (order.kind !== "tco_removal") return [`${c}: sent ${at.toISOString()}.`];
      const [clock] = await rows<{ clock_start: string | null }>(tx, sql`select ${isoOf("clock_start")} as clock_start from public.legal_order_clock where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      return [`${c}: sent ${at.toISOString()}; the clock starts ${clock?.clock_start ?? at.toISOString()}.`];
    }
    case "order-due": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (order.kind === "tco_removal") refuse(c, "a removal order's deadline is its hour, from its receipt");
      const word = cmd.positional[0];
      const at = word === "none" ? null : instant(c, word);
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set due_at = ${at?.toISOString() ?? null}::timestamptz where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "due_set", { dueAt: at?.toISOString() ?? null });
      return [at === null ? `${c}: no deadline.` : `${c}: due ${at.toISOString()}.`];
    }
    case "order-verify": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const how = freeText(c, "--how", flag(cmd, "--how")!);
      const [row] = await rows<{ verified_at: string; items: number }>(
        tx,
        sql`update public.legal_orders o set verified_at = now(), verified_how = ${how} where o.id = ${order.id}::uuid
            returning ${isoOf("o.verified_at")} as verified_at, (select count(*)::int from public.legal_order_items i where i.order_id = o.id) as items`,
      );
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "verified", { verifiedAt: row!.verified_at, howSha256: sha256(how) });
      return [`${c}: order ${order.id} verified at ${row!.verified_at}: ${row!.items} items compared with the order.`];
    }
    case "order-issued": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const at = instant(c, cmd.positional[0]);
      if (at.getTime() > Date.parse(order.receivedAt ?? order.openedAt)) refuse(c, "an order is not issued after it was received");
      if (order.sectionC && (order.released || order.holdEndedAt !== null)) refuse(c, "the author's notice was already released, or its hold was ended");
      // While a notice of the order is held, a time stamp whose computed end is not ahead would release it within minutes,
      // which cannot be taken back: nothing changes then unless --release says that is what the order says.
      const [held] = await rows<{ held: boolean; would_end: string; past: boolean }>(
        tx,
        sql`select (o.section_c and public.order_hold_until(o.id) > clock_timestamp()
                    and exists (select 1 from public.legal_order_items i join public.decisions d on d.order_item_id = i.id where i.order_id = o.id and d.informed_at is null)) as held,
                   ${isoOf("least(public.order_hold_end(x.at, o.hold_extended), o.authority_hold_until)")} as would_end,
                   least(public.order_hold_end(x.at, o.hold_extended), o.authority_hold_until) <= clock_timestamp() as past
              from public.legal_orders o cross join (select ${at.toISOString()}::timestamptz as at) x where o.id = ${order.id}::uuid`,
      );
      if (order.kind === "tco_removal" && held!.held && held!.past && !cmd.flags.has("--release")) {
        throw new Refusal(
          `${c}: with this date the hold would have ended on ${held!.would_end}, and the author would be told at the next dispatch round. Nothing changed; give --release if that is what the order says.`,
        );
      }
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set issued_at = ${at.toISOString()}::timestamptz where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "issued_at_set", { issuedAt: at.toISOString(), release: cmd.flags.has("--release") });
      return [`${c}: issued ${at.toISOString()}; the notice is ${await holdWords(tx, order.id)}.`];
    }
    case "order-texts": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const which = (["--reasons", "--redress", "--scope"] as const).filter((name) => cmd.flags.has(name));
      if (which.length !== 1) refuse(c, "give exactly one of --reasons, --redress and --scope");
      const column = which[0]!.slice(2) as "reasons" | "redress" | "scope";
      if (column === "scope" && order.kind === "tco_removal") refuse(c, "a removal order has no territorial scope of its own to record");
      const text = stdin!.toString("utf8").replace(/[ ]*$/, "");
      const max = column === "scope" ? ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.short : ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.long;
      if (!(text as string & { isWellFormed(): boolean }).isWellFormed() || hasControl(text, true) || FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text) || text.trim() === "") {
        refuse(c, "the text from standard input holds a control or an invisible character, or no text");
      }
      if (Array.from(text).length > max) refuse(c, `the text has more than ${max} characters`);
      const salt = randomBytes(32).toString("hex");
      const digest = await textDigest(salt, text);
      await tx.execute(
        column === "reasons"
          ? sql`update public.legal_orders set reasons = ${text}, reasons_salt = ${salt}, reasons_digest = ${digest} where id = ${order.id}::uuid`
          : column === "redress"
            ? sql`update public.legal_orders set redress = ${text}, redress_salt = ${salt}, redress_digest = ${digest} where id = ${order.id}::uuid`
            : sql`update public.legal_orders set scope = ${text}, scope_salt = ${salt}, scope_digest = ${digest} where id = ${order.id}::uuid`,
      );
      // Task 3 (section 7.7, step 3): every told order decision of the order is owed its mail again, so that the dispatch
      // round mails order_notice_added: a time limit of the author's runs from receiving the authority's words. The event's
      // time is the recorded instant, which the notice prints; no column holds it a second time.
      const told = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        tx,
        sql`update public.decisions d set author_mail = 'pending'
              from public.legal_order_items i
             where i.order_id = ${order.id}::uuid and d.order_item_id = i.id and d.kind::text = 'order' and d.informed_at is not null and d.author_mail <> 'none'
            returning d.id`,
      );
      const [held] = await rows<{ held: number; until: string | null }>(
        tx,
        sql`select count(*)::int as held, ${isoOf("min(public.order_hold_until(i.order_id))")} as until
              from public.legal_order_items i join public.decisions d on d.order_item_id = i.id
             where i.order_id = ${order.id}::uuid and d.kind::text = 'order' and d.informed_at is null`,
      );
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "texts_recorded", { text: column, digest, authors: told.length });
      const head = `${c}: ${column} recorded (${Array.from(text).length} characters).`;
      if (told.length > 0) return [`${head} ${told.length} authors are sent an email that the notice has grown; the notice shows the text and this time from now.`];
      if (held!.held > 0) return [`${head} The notice is held: it will show the text once it is released, ${held!.until ?? "at a time not recorded yet"}.`];
      return [`${head} No author has been told of this order: the notice shows the text from its first telling.`];
    }
    case "order-document": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (stdin!.length === 0) refuse(c, "standard input held no document");
      const digest = sha256(stdin!);
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set document_sha256 = ${digest}, document_bytes = ${stdin!.length} where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "document_recorded", { documentSha256: digest, documentBytes: stdin!.length });
      return [`${c}: ${digest}, ${stdin!.length} bytes.`];
    }
    case "order-scrutiny": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (order.kind !== "tco_removal") refuse(c, "only a removal order from another Member State is put to scrutiny");
      const step = cmd.positional[0];
      const at = instant(c, flag(cmd, "--at")!);
      if (at.getTime() > Date.now()) refuse(c, "--at is in the future");
      if (step === "requested") {
        const by = flag(cmd, "--by")!;
        if (by !== "korbat" && by !== "author") refuse(c, "--by is korbat or author");
        await recorded(tx, order.id, "scrutiny_requested", { by, at: at.toISOString() }, { effectiveAt: at });
        return [`${c}: request recorded.`];
      }
      if (step === "decided") {
        const outcome = flag(cmd, "--outcome")!;
        if (!(SCRUTINY_OUTCOMES as readonly string[]).includes(outcome)) refuse(c, "--outcome is upheld or annulled");
        await recorded(tx, order.id, "scrutiny_decided", { outcome, at: at.toISOString() }, { ground: outcome, effectiveAt: at });
        return [outcome === "annulled" ? `${c}: decided: annulled. An admin reinstates each item on its case, ground scrutiny, at once.` : `${c}: decided: upheld. The order stands.`];
      }
      return refuse(c, "say requested or decided");
    }
    case "order-reopen": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const how = freeText(c, "--how", flag(cmd, "--how")!);
      if (order.closedAt === null) refuse(c, "the order is not closed");
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set closed_at = null where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "reopened", { howSha256: sha256(how) });
      return [`${c}: order ${order.id} is open again. Its times are unchanged.`];
    }
    case "order-tell-rule": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (order.kind !== "dsa_art10") refuse(c, "only an order to provide information has this rule; a DSA Article 9 order's is its hold (order-hold-until)");
      const when = flag(cmd, "--when", false);
      if (when === null) {
        const fallback = settings.homeState === null ? null : (STATE_FACTS[settings.homeState as MemberState]?.tellPersonDefault ?? null);
        throw new Refusal(`${c}: the home state's default is ${fallback === null ? "not filled in" : fallback}; give --when to record a rule; nothing changed`);
      }
      const basis = freeText(c, "--basis", flag(cmd, "--basis")!);
      const rule: TellPersonRule = when === "at_effect" || when === "never" ? when : "at_instant";
      const at = rule === "at_instant" ? instant(c, when) : null;
      await tx.execute(
        sql`update public.legal_orders set tell_person = ${rule}, tell_person_at = ${at?.toISOString() ?? null}::timestamptz, hold_basis = ${basis} where id = ${order.id}::uuid`,
      );
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "tell_person_set", { rule, at: at?.toISOString() ?? null, basisSha256: sha256(basis) });
      return [`${c}: the person is told ${rule === "at_effect" ? "at effect" : rule === "never" ? "never" : `at ${at!.toISOString()}`}, on the basis recorded.`];
    }
    case "order-hold-until": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (order.kind === "dsa_art10") refuse(c, "an order to provide information has no notice of korbat's: its rule for telling the person is order-tell-rule's");
      if (!order.sectionC) refuse(c, "no notice of this order is held");
      if (order.released || order.holdEndedAt !== null) refuse(c, "the author's notice was already released, or its hold was ended");
      const word = cmd.positional[0];
      const at = word === "none" ? null : instant(c, word);
      const basis = freeText(c, "--basis", flag(cmd, "--basis")!);
      const how = freeText(c, "--how", flag(cmd, "--how")!);
      if (order.kind === "tco_removal" && at === null) refuse(c, "a removal order's hold has the Regulation's end: give the authority's instant, or leave its end as computed");
      // The end this record would leave (the lesser of the computed end and the authority's for a removal order; the
      // authority's own for a DSA order), and whether it is no longer ahead: that would release the notice within minutes.
      const [would] = await rows<{ until: string | null; past: boolean; computed: string | null; computed_wins: boolean }>(
        tx,
        sql`select ${isoOf("w.until")} as until, coalesce(w.until <= clock_timestamp(), false) as past, ${isoOf("w.computed")} as computed,
                   coalesce(w.computed < x.at, false) as computed_wins
              from public.legal_orders o
              cross join (select ${at?.toISOString() ?? null}::timestamptz as at) x
              cross join lateral (select case when o.kind = 'tco_removal' then public.order_hold_end(coalesce(o.issued_at, o.received_at, o.opened_at), o.hold_extended) end as computed) c
              cross join lateral (select case when o.kind = 'tco_removal' then least(c.computed, x.at) else x.at end as until, c.computed) w
             where o.id = ${order.id}::uuid`,
      );
      if (would!.until !== null && would!.past && !cmd.flags.has("--release")) {
        throw new Refusal(`${c}: with this end the hold would have ended on ${would!.until}, and the author would be told at the next dispatch round. Nothing changed; give --release if that is what the order says.`);
      }
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set authority_hold_until = ${at?.toISOString() ?? null}::timestamptz, hold_basis = ${basis} where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "hold_until_set", { until: at?.toISOString() ?? null, basisSha256: sha256(basis), howSha256: sha256(how), release: cmd.flags.has("--release") });
      if (at === null) return [`${c}: the notice is held with no end. Every staff account is reminded daily until an end is recorded.`];
      if (order.kind === "tco_removal" && would!.computed_wins) return [`${c}: the computed end ${would!.computed} is earlier and stands.`];
      return [`${c}: the notice is held until ${would!.until}.`];
    }
    case "order-hold-extend": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (order.kind !== "tco_removal") refuse(c, "only a removal order's hold is extended once; a DSA order's later time is order-hold-until's");
      if (!order.sectionC) refuse(c, "no notice of this order is held");
      if (order.released || order.holdEndedAt !== null) refuse(c, "the author's notice was already released, or its hold was ended");
      const received = instant(c, flag(cmd, "--received")!);
      if (received.getTime() > Date.now()) refuse(c, "--received is in the future");
      const how = freeText(c, "--how", flag(cmd, "--how")!);
      const [prior] = await rows<{ extended: boolean; console_at: string | null; cli: boolean }>(
        tx,
        sql`select o.hold_extended as extended,
                   ${isoOf("(select max(e.at) from public.legal_order_events e where e.order_id = o.id and e.kind = 'hold_extended' and e.via = 'console')")} as console_at,
                   exists (select 1 from public.legal_order_events e where e.order_id = o.id and e.kind = 'hold_extended' and e.via = 'cli') as cli
              from public.legal_orders o where o.id = ${order.id}::uuid`,
      );
      if (prior!.cli) refuse(c, "the non-disclosure period was already extended once");
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_extended = true where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "hold_extended", { received: received.toISOString(), howSha256: sha256(how), confirms: prior!.console_at }, { effectiveAt: received });
      const until = await holdWords(tx, order.id);
      if (prior!.console_at !== null) return [`${c}: the console's extension of ${prior!.console_at} is confirmed; the notice is ${until}.`];
      return [`${c}: the notice is ${until}. It cannot be extended again.`];
    }
    case "order-hold-end": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      const reason = flag(cmd, "--reason")!;
      if (!(HOLD_END_REASONS as readonly string[]).includes(reason)) refuse(c, "--reason is not_authentic, annulled, released_by_authority or not_ordered");
      const how = freeText(c, "--how", flag(cmd, "--how")!);
      if (!order.sectionC || order.released || order.holdEndedAt !== null) refuse(c, "no notice of this order is held");
      // An extension the console recorded that turns out not to be the authority's is undone only once the first period
      // has ended: ending the hold before that day would tell early.
      const [first] = await rows<{ ahead: boolean; extended: boolean }>(
        tx,
        sql`select o.hold_extended as extended,
                   coalesce(o.kind = 'tco_removal' and o.hold_extended
                            and least(public.order_hold_end(coalesce(o.issued_at, o.received_at, o.opened_at), false), o.authority_hold_until) > clock_timestamp(), false) as ahead
              from public.legal_orders o where o.id = ${order.id}::uuid`,
      );
      if (reason === "not_ordered" && first!.extended && first!.ahead) refuse(c, "the first period of this extended hold has not ended: ending it now as not ordered would tell early");
      const [ended] = await rows<{ at: string }>(
        tx,
        sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = now(), hold_end_reason = ${reason} where id = ${order.id}::uuid returning ${isoOf("hold_ended_at")} as at`,
      );
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "hold_ended", { reason, howSha256: sha256(how) }, { ground: reason });
      return [`${c}: the hold ended at ${ended!.at}. The next dispatch round tells the author, within about 10 minutes.`];
    }
    case "order-preserve-extend":
      return preserveExtend(tx, cmd);
    case "order-access":
      return preservedAccess(tx, cmd);
    case "order-told": {
      const order = await lockOrder(tx, c, cmd.order!);
      if (order.kind !== "dsa_art10") refuse(c, "only the person an order to provide information names is told this way");
      if (order.tellPerson === null) refuse(c, "whether the person may be told of this order is not recorded: run staff.js order-tell-rule first");
      if (order.tellPerson === "never") refuse(c, "the rule recorded for this order is that the person is never told");
      if (order.tellPerson === "at_instant" && Date.parse(order.tellPersonAt!) > Date.now()) refuse(c, `the person may be told only from ${order.tellPersonAt}`);
      const at = instant(c, flag(cmd, "--at")!);
      if (at.getTime() > Date.now()) refuse(c, "--at is in the future");
      const how = freeText(c, "--how", flag(cmd, "--how")!);
      await recorded(tx, order.id, "person_told", { at: at.toISOString(), howSha256: sha256(how) }, { effectiveAt: at });
      return [`${c}: recorded at ${at.toISOString()}.`];
    }
  }
}

/** order-open (section 8.11): the rows of insertOrder as the migrator, the alert order_opened, then the audit row. */
async function open(tx: DbTx, cmd: OrderCommand, settings: OrderSettings): Promise<string[]> {
  const c = cmd.command;
  if (settings.homeState === null || settings.appOrigin === null) throw new Refusal(`${c}: HOME_STATE and APP_ORIGIN must be set for the migrate service; nothing changed`);
  if (cmd.positional.length > 0) refuse(c, `${cmd.positional[0]} is not a flag of order-open`);
  const kind = flag(cmd, "--kind")! as OrderKind;
  if (!(ORDER_KINDS as readonly string[]).includes(kind)) refuse(c, "--kind is tco_removal, dsa_art9 or dsa_art10");
  const state = MemberStateCode.safeParse(flag(cmd, "--state"));
  if (!state.success) refuse(c, "--state is the issuing Member State's two-letter code");
  const authority = OrderAuthority.safeParse(flag(cmd, "--authority"));
  if (!authority.success) refuse(c, "--authority is one line of 1 to 200 characters");
  const reference = OrderReference.safeParse(flag(cmd, "--reference"));
  if (!reference.success) refuse(c, "--reference is one line of 1 to 200 characters");
  const channel = flag(cmd, "--channel")! as OrderChannel;
  if (!(ORDER_CHANNELS as readonly string[]).includes(channel)) refuse(c, "--channel is mailbox, portal, post or other");
  const messageId = flag(cmd, "--message", false);
  if (messageId !== null && !/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/.test(messageId)) refuse(c, "--message is a message's id");
  if (messageId !== null && channel !== "mailbox") refuse(c, "an order whose message is listed arrived by mail: --channel mailbox");
  if (messageId !== null && cmd.flags.has("--received")) refuse(c, "a listed message's time of receipt is its own: give --message or --received, not both");
  const receivedWord = flag(cmd, "--received", false);
  const sentWord = flag(cmd, "--sent", false);
  const receivedAt = receivedWord === null ? null : instant(c, receivedWord);
  const sentAt = sentWord === null ? null : instant(c, sentWord);
  const links = cmd.flags.get("--link") ?? [];
  if (kind === "dsa_art10" ? links.length > 0 : links.length === 0) refuse(c, "an order to provide information takes no --link; the other kinds take at least one");
  if (links.length > ORDER_ITEMS_MAX) refuse(c, `an order holds at most ${ORDER_ITEMS_MAX} links`);
  if (links.some((link) => !OrderLinkText.safeParse(link).success)) refuse(c, "a --link is one line of at most 500 characters");
  if (new Set(links).size !== links.length) refuse(c, "a --link is named twice");
  const sectionC = cmd.flags.has("--section-c");
  // --section-c forces --withhold, as the console and the database do; a removal order always withholds.
  const withhold = cmd.flags.has("--withhold") || sectionC || kind === "tco_removal";
  if (messageId !== null && (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from public.contact_messages where id = ${messageId}::uuid`)).length === 0) {
    refuse(c, `no message has the id ${messageId}`);
  }
  let items;
  try {
    items = await orderItemsFor(tx, settings.appOrigin, links);
  } catch {
    return refuse(c, "two links name the same post");
  }
  const id = randomUUID();
  const crossBorder = state.data !== settings.homeState;
  let inserted;
  try {
    inserted = await tx.transaction(async (inner) =>
      insertOrder(inner, {
        id,
        kind,
        memberState: state.data!,
        authority: authority.data!,
        reference: reference.data!,
        channel,
        messageId,
        sectionC,
        emergency: cmd.flags.has("--emergency"),
        crossBorder,
        withholdFromAuthor: withhold,
        openedBy: null,
        items,
        cli: { receivedAt, sentAt },
      }),
    );
  } catch (err) {
    const code = (err as { cause?: { code?: string; constraint_name?: string } }).cause;
    if (code?.code === "23505" && code.constraint_name === "legal_orders_reference_key") return refuse(c, "an order of this authority with this reference is already recorded (order_exists)");
    if (code?.code === "23514") return refuse(c, "a time of receipt or of sending after now is not taken");
    throw err;
  }
  const dueAt = kind === "tco_removal" && inserted.receivedAt !== null ? deadlineOf(inserted.receivedAt.toISOString()) : null;
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS.order_opened;
```
